LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch as these two teams take center stage on "Thursday Night Football" after Week 7 losses IMAGN Images via Reuters Connect In the Week 8 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Green Bay Packers play host to the Carolina Panthers . The Packers enter this game off a disappointing loss to the division rival Detroit Lions , in a game they had multiple chances to win. Green Bay had won three in a row to salvage its season after a blowout loss to the Atlanta Falcons the last time the Packers played on Thursday night (Week 3), but they hit a bump in the road last week. Now, they're looking to make it four wins in five games. The Panthers are coming off an embarrassing blowout loss at the hands of the division rival Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Carolina was blasted 43-13 last week and was never truly competitive, falling down 17-0 early. However, the Panthers still sit at .500 after climbing that hump with their win over the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 6. Now, they try to get back to their winning ways. Which of these two teams will get back in the win column? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Packers vs. Panthers live Date: Thursday, Oct. 29 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Lambeau Field (Green Bay) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Packers -3/5, O/U 47.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Panthers have the ball The Panthers limped to their worst offensive performance of the season last week, managing just 266 yards, 15 first downs and 13 points while turning the ball over four times. They had previously gained at least 340 yards in every game, gained at least 24 first downs in four of five, and scored 25-plus points in four of five. Bryce Young returned to poor form on Sunday, going only 14-of-27 for 163 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, while also fumbling once. He's now completed south of 52% of his passes in back-to-back games and south of 55% in three of his last four, with the only exception being a game against the decrepit Lions pass defense. Young got off to a hot start to the season , but he's cooled off a bit as of late. The Packers have been a tough matchup for opposing quarterbacks this year. They're eighth in net passing yards per attempt, and they've yet to allow more than 296 net passing yards in any game this season. They've also allowed just nine touchdown passes against nine interceptions. Jonathan Gannon has been good at limiting what opponents can do through the air, for the most part. It is, however, worth noting that the Packers faced Carson Wentz , Geno Smith , Michael Penix Jr. , Jalon Daniels and Tyson Bagent before getting Dak Prescott and Jared Goff over the last two weeks. So they haven't exactly done this against a murderer's row of opponents. Green Bay has gotten pressure at a below-average rate — no surprise with Micah Parsons still sidelined. Instead, the Packers have gotten by against the pass with sticky coverage and timely plays on the ball. Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse have been solid on the outside. Javon Bullard has played well in the slot, and the safeties are providing quality help over the top and in the middle of the field. Carolina's passing game is mostly built outside the numbers with Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker , though Young has thrown over the middle more this season than in past years. It'll be up to the skyscrapers on the perimeter to win their one-on-one matchups here in order to give Young room to throw, though he should have more time than he did last week thanks to Green Bay's relatively weaker pass rush. In the run game, the Panthers lean on Chuba Hubbard , who is averaging 4.8 yards per carry in a workhorse role in the absence of Jonathon Brooks . Hubbard only got seven carries in the negative game script last week, but you can likely expect the Panthers to try to "Establish The Run" here as a way to get their offense back on track. Green Bay has allowed only 3.9 yards per carry this season, though, so it might be tough, especially with right tackle Taylor Moton now on the sidelines. When the Packers have the ball The Packers welcomed Josh Jacobs back to the lineup last week but still found themselves entirely unable to run the ball against the Lions. They totaled just 60 yards on the ground, with Jacobs himself carrying 11 times for only 36 yards. Green Bay is now averaging a pathetic 2.9 yards per carry on the season, which unsurprisingly ranks dead last in the league. The Panthers, meanwhile, were run over by the Bucs last week. Bucky Irving and Co. blew past Carolina for a remarkable 258 yards on the ground, which was made all the more incredible by the fact that the Panthers had yielded just 81 rushing yards in their previous two games combined. Still, Carolina has allowed 5.2 yards per carry on the season now, which, to no surprise, ranks dead last. Almost 60% of the rushing yards the Panthers have allowed, though, came in their games against the Bucs and the Chicago Bears in Week 1. They've been fine-ish against the run otherwise. So, can the Packers run the ball with any degree of success here? If the recent history of this season is any indication, then the answer is probably not. Jacobs has been at or below 4.0 yards per carry in two of his last three full seasons, and spending six weeks on the commissioner's exempt list in the wake of a disturbing domestic violence incident probably didn't make him a more efficient runner. And the offensive line is still not a good run-blocking unit. So, the fate of the Packers' offense likely once again falls on the right shoulder of Jordan Love . Love has only completed 59.8% of his passes at an average of 7.4 yards per attempt this season, but he's been victimized by a league-high 21 drops, according to Tru Media. Love is attacking deep downfield consistently, with a 9.1-yard average depth of throw that ranks fourth-highest in the NFL . As such, he's created explosive plays (16-plus-yard gains) at the third-highest rate in the league among 33 qualified quarterbacks. He should see favorable matchups when he looks downfield on Thursday night. Panthers starting cornerbacks Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson remain out on injured reserve, which has left rookie Will Lee III and Akayleb Evans as the starting corners. But Evans is also out on Thursday night, meaning, well, I honestly don't even know who is going to step up in his absence. The Panthers elevated Marco Wilson from the practice squad, and they may need to shift Chau Smith-Wade outside. Either way, it's not a great situation for Carolina. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden , who is trending to play, should be able to find space down the field against these corners, and then it's just a matter of actually hanging onto the ball when Love puts it on them. Green Bay could have a big night through the air if the Packers can protect Love, which will be made easier by the absence of Panthers edge rusher Jaelan Phillips , who is also out for this game. It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Watson and Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better as of late after a rough start to the season. The Minnesota Vikings are the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, as the San Francisco 49ers were handed their first loss by the Atlanta Falcons , while the Kansas City Chiefs took their first "L" to the Seattle Seahawks . The Vikings have a massive matchup this week, as they take on the high-flying Lions in Detroit. Elsewhere around the NFL , Lamar Jackson looks to make his return to the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills , the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers face off for the second time in the last month, and the Chicago Bears travel out west to play Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. Which teams should you pick in Week 8, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 27 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Packers -3.5): I'm willing to overlook the Carolina Panthers ' surprising 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They are a better team than what they showed last Sunday, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that Carolina's rushing defense ranks dead last in the NFL with 153.2 yards allowed per game. Josh Jacobs rushed for just 36 yards on 11 carries last week against the Lions in his 2026 debut, but I think he's in for a massive homecoming in primetime on a short week. I'm not saying the Packers run away with this one, but I'll take them to cover 3.5 points. … Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 23 Dubin (Packers -3.5): It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better of late after a rough start to the season. … Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Dajani ( Ravens +3.5): Ignore that Baltimore allowed 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals last week, because it appears that Lamar Jackson is back! He was playing some legitimate MVP-level ball before getting hurt, as Jackson went 3-1 as the starter, while completing 70.8% of his passes with 10.1 yards per attempt, six passing touchdowns and just one interception. Only four quarterbacks have put up those kinds of numbers in their first four starts of a season in the past 40 years. The Ravens are a completely different team with Jackson under center, and this Bills defense allows too many points. Buffalo ranks third-worst in scoring defense (28.5 ppg), and has allowed at least 30 points in four of its five victories this season. Jackson is 10-5 SU and 13-2 ATS as an underdog in his career. He's statistically the best quarterback to bet on when listed as an underdog since 1970. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bills 28 Dubin (Ravens +3.5): This is the same deal as with the Ravens and me pretty much every week: flip the pick if Lamar Jackson sits out again. Otherwise, I like the Ravens to at least keep things close against the Bills. Both of these offenses have been pretty excellent, and the Ravens have been especially so when Jackson has been on the field with Zay Flowers . Ultimately, though, the Bills' home-field advantage and the weaknesses in Baltimore's own pass defense lead me to take the Bills to win and the Ravens to cover. … Prediction: Bills 30, Ravens 27 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani (Lions -3): I'm shocked by this line, honestly. The only remaining undefeated team in the NFL is a three-point underdog to a division rival? With that said, I think I agree with it. The Vikings' defense is the main reason they are 5-0, as they've allowed a league-leading 12.3 points per game, plus registered a league-leading 10.6% sack rate and 47.6% pressure rate. Offensively, the Vikings have the fewest touchdowns (10) by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions and rank 31st in offensive EPA. They could have lost last week to the Indianapolis Colts , who are in the midst of a fire sale. As for the Lions, the concern has always been with their defense. But I think Kelvin Sheppard 's unit is coming along. They allowed just 17 points to the Packers last week, and Brian Branch is back in the lineup. Maybe we could see a push here, but I'm taking the Lions to win … Prediction: Lions 24, Vikings 20 Dubin (Lions -3): Detroit has recently been thrown off its offensive game by Brian Flores' defense, but the offense is operating at an extremely high level right now, with Jared Goff playing as well as he has in recent memory. And as Dajani said, this Minnesota offense just does not have the ability to get into a high-scoring game and come away with a win. They need the defense to hold the opponent down entirely, and I'm not sure that even Flores' bunch can do that in the friendly confines of Ford Field. … Prediction: Lions 23, Vikings 14 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) Dajani (Steelers -3.5): How can the Browns keep getting away with this? They overcame a 14-0 deficit in Nashville on Sunday, as Harold Fannin Jr . took a short reception 36 yards down the field with 20 seconds remaining to set up a 32-yard game-winning field goal from Andre Szmyt . Deshaun Watson became the third quarterback since 1970 to register a game-winning drive in each of his team's first five wins of the season. With this being a divisional game against an opponent that just got back from Paris, I can understand why some would take the points with the underdog given the hook. But the Steelers are 3-0 ATS at home. That includes Week 3, when they dropped 30 points on Joe Burrow and the Bengals in a win, and Week 5, when Pittsburgh scored 34 points in a double-digit victory over the Colts. The Steelers are averaging 26.0 points per game over their last five contests, which ranks top 10 in the NFL, and are 8-0 SU and ATS in their last eight home games vs. the Browns. In fact, Pittsburgh is actually a perfect 11-0 ATS in its last 11 home divisional games. Insane stat. … Prediction: Steelers 26, Browns 21 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): I don't understand how the Browns keep doing it. Every single one of their victories has required a game-winning drive in the final five minutes of the game. That's not sustainable on any level whatsoever. The Steelers don't exactly have consistency written all over them, considering the vagaries of their passing game and the fact that their three-game winning streak has come against weak opponents. However, I trust Jaylen Warren and Co. more than I do the Browns at this point. … Prediction: Steelers 20, Browns 13 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) Dajani (Falcons +2.5): I have plenty of questions about both of these teams, but I did tell you the Falcons were going to cover the small number vs. the 49ers last week! Atlanta finished that game on a 26-6 run after trailing 14-3. They scored on four straight drives. I'm not sure the Buccaneers deserve to be three-point favorites this week after that destruction of the Panthers. Baker Mayfield had to throw for just 64 yards and a touchdown in a 43-13 victory, as Bucky Irving , Kenneth Gainwell and Sean Tucker combined for 246 yards rushing and three touchdowns. This Falcons rush defense ranks fourth in the NFL with 88.9 rushing yards allowed per game. Plus, the Falcons have won two road games this season by 20+ points after being listed as an underdog, and are 4-0 ATS in their last four road games against the Buccaneers. … Prediction: Falcons 26, Buccaneers 24 Dubin (Falcons +2.5): The Buccaneers ran all over the Panthers last week, but Atlanta has actually been quite good against the run, allowing only 3.8 yards per carry this season. Can Tampa really control the game with Bucky Irving the way it did last week, or will it have to actually turn Baker Mayfield loose as a passer here? If the Bucs have to do that, I have more confidence in Atlanta's offense right now, with Bijan Robinson , Drake London and even Kyle Pitts contributing at a high level. … Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 17 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Dajani ( Broncos +1.5): The Broncos had an embarrassing outing last time they played the Chiefs, allowing 247 yards off of 28 missed tackles in a 31-10 loss. There has been a lot of talk about Bo Nix and the offense, but what about the Chiefs? They averaged 4.3 yards per play and recorded just 213 yards of total offense in that embarrassing loss to the Seahawks. The team seemingly never got off the bus. Green Bay is set as a 3.5-point favorite at home in this primetime matchup, and it’s looking to stay over .500 in the 2026 season after a Week 7 loss to Detroit. Despite a three-game winning streak earlier this season and a 4-3 record overall, the Packers are in last place in the NFC North heading into Week 8. So, every game means a ton for Jordan Love, Matt LaFleur and Co. as they look to get back to the playoffs. Bryce Young and the Panthers are in a different spot, as they’re in first place in the weak NFC South despite going 3-3 through their first six games. Carolina lost at home to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 7, and it only has a half-game lead over the Atlanta Falcons in the division. The Panthers won the NFC South last season, but a litany of injuries to open the 2026 campaign have put them in a tough spot to repeat. Still, oddsmakers aren’t expecting them to have another blowout loss with this spread set inside a touchdown on Thursday. All week long, the SI Betting team has shared our favorite game picks, props, anytime touchdown scorer selections and more for Panthers vs. Packers. The Packers' defense ranks 12th in opponent EPA per play and 10th in opponent EPA per dropback, so with them being on their home field on a short week, I expect them to get to Young in this game. I'll take the Packers to cover on Thursday Night Football. Packers running back Josh Jacobs missed the first six weeks of the season on the Commissioner's Exempt List, but he returned in Week 7 and made an immediate impact against the Detroit Lions. Jacobs played just 52.2 percent of Green Bay’s offense snaps, but he saw 18 opportunities (11 rushes, seven targets) and ended up finding the end zone. The former first-round pick had 11 carries for 36 yards and caught five of his seven targets for 55 yards (and a receiving score) in the loss to Detroit. He has a great matchup against a Carolina defense that is 30th in EPA/Rush, 32nd in yards per carry allowed and 32nd in rushing touchdowns allowed (11) this season. While this isn’t the most favorable price, Jacobs has been a touchdown machine in his Packers career, scoring 31 times in 33 games. He’s an easy bet against one of the worst run defenses in the NFL. Bryce Young has been one of the best passers in the NFL even with his rough showing in Week 7 against Tampa Bay. In six games, Young has thrown for 1,712 yards and 12 scores, reaching at least 281 passing yards in five of his six games. He’s also posted four games with multiple touchdown passes. They lined Amon-Ra St. Brown – usually their slot receiver – outside quite a bit, and he finished the day 153 receiving yards. Plus, deep-ball threat Jameson Williams had two scores and 91 yards in the win. So, I expect Young and the Panthers to air it out against Green Bay, which has still allowed nine passing scores this season. Young has 36 or more pass attempts in five of his six games, so I think he’s a strong bounce-back candidate after a weird Week 7 game got out of hand very quickly for Carolina. Love has thrown the ball quite a bit in the 2026 season, and former first-round pick Matthew Golden has been one of the biggest beneficiaries. Through seven games, Golden has 69 targets, 36 catches and 540 receiving yards. He’s also found the end zone three times. Now, Love and Golden haven’t connected as much as you’d expect given his target share, but the second-year wideout still has five games with at least five receptions. Golden also has six or more targets in every game and four games with 12 or more looks. So, the volume should be there against a Carolina defense that is pretty average against the pass (13th in EPA/Pass) this season. I think Golden is undervalued at this number in Week 8. picks.blurb: Predictions: Will Packers Score Thursday Night Bounce-Back vs. Panthers? It couldn’t possibly go worse than when they lost to the Falcons 35-14 on Thursday night last month. “Yeah, I should change everything, huh?” defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon sort-of joked on Wednesday, “because we laid an egg – me I’m talking about. I hold that to ourselves. I think Matt (LaFleur) made some tweaks, which I really liked. I think it’s going to help our guys. We’ll see, the proof will be in the pudding.” The Packers need to find a victory in the pudding against Carolina. Green Bay is in last place in the NFC North and holds a tenuous grip on the final spot in the NFC. Obviously, it’s early to be overly concerned about the playoff race, but the division race is in danger of getting away from them before the calendar flips to November. Will the Packers win? Here are our weekly predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Panthers Prediction The Packers and Panthers are two of the most beat-up teams in the NFL , a fact complicated by playing on a Thursday. The injuries are probably one reason why these also are among the most inconsistent teams in the league. It seems like the Packers have a lot of injuries. But is that true? Here's some good injury data shared by @RotoWire . ⬇️ https://t.co/Mp2IlrCeZW The Packers can’t get out of their own way on offense, which is why they’ve scored 20 or fewer points in four of seven games. They scored only 17 points last week against the Lions, who have one of the worst defenses in the NFL. Detroit entered the game on pace to blow away the dubious league record for passing yards allowed. Jordan Love and Co. failed miserably to capitalize, especially in key moments. The Panthers are no better. Remember Green Bay’s loss to Atlanta at Lambeau? That came just days after Carolina went into Atlanta and won by 31. The Panthers had won three of their last four games until getting steamrolled 43-13 by the Buccaneers. So, which team(s) will show up tonight? So, let’s bring it back to injuries. The Panthers’ starting cornerbacks, Mike Jackson and Jaycee Horn, are on injured reserve. Their best pass rusher, Jaelan Phillips, will be inactive due to injury. So, there should be opportunities for the Packers to make plays in the passing game. Combined with a matchup against the worst run defense in the NFL, this could be a breakout game for Green Bay’s offense. “Should be,” of course, is the operative phrase. The only thing the Packers do consistently is play inconsistently. They can’t run the football. They struggle to protect the passer. They drop passes. They misfire on third down and squander opportunities in the red zone. So, should the Packers have a big game offensively? Yes. But will they? At least the defense is good, with Gannon earning his paycheck by fielding a formidable unit that has mostly played winning football even though it can’t rush the passer with a traditional four-man rush. So, who wins? I’d give the advantages to Green Bay on both sides of the ball. On offense, Love should have a strong game against Carolina’s depleted pass defense. Heck, they might even be able to run the football against the league’s worst rush defense. On defense, the Packers have spoken highly of Panthers quarterback Bryce Young all week, but Young is not as good as Detroit’s Jared Goff and the Panthers have only one big-time threat in the passing game compared to two for Detroit. The Panthers will be without their preferred starting offensive tackles, too. So, the Packers will score a key win. A 5-3 start with Micah Parsons still not back on the practice field would be a major victory for a team that has aspirations to be playing deep into January. Bill’s Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 17. Bill’s Record: 5-2. Here are the 10 most important Packers for tonight's game, a story filled with quotes and other good stuff by @JacobWestendorf . ⬇️ https://t.co/tX2pc7MrfW Jacob Westendorf’s Packers-Panthers Prediction I don't think this game is going to be pretty. Matt LaFleur said earlier this week that Panthers coordinator Ejiro Evero's defense forces everyone on offense to be consistent on every single play. The Packers have not been like that all season. The injuries on the offensive line make for some uncertainty, and give this coaching staff a chance to screw up the starting five combination, like they have so many times in the past. That being said, Carolina is missing some big guns on defense, including their star pass rusher. Even if Matthew Golden cannot go or is on limited reps, Christian Watson and Tucker Kraft should be able to make enough plays in the passing game. Perhaps Josh Jacobs can finally find some room to roam on the ground against the league's worst run defense. Expect a sloppy game, but the Packers will make one more play than the Panthers, getting them to 5-3 before a much-needed mini bye week. Jacob’s Prediction: Packers 17, Panthers 14. away.headline: Bucs-Panthers Inactives | Baker Mayfield Returns to Action
away.blurb: After missing three games due to a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand, quarterback Baker Mayfield is back in the lineup for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday as they take on the Carolina Panthers in a critical intra-division game. Mayfield carried a questionable designation on the injury report into the weekend but was able to practice without limitations throughout the week. He intends to wear a specialized glove on his right hand that offers added support to the injured joint, preventing the thumb from being bent backward. Mayfield will not have the team's top receiving target at his disposal, however, as wide receiver Emeka Egbuka is out for Week Seven with both a concussion and a foot injury. In addition, starting right tackle Luke Goedeke is out due to a calf ailment and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. will miss his third straight outing thanks to a rib fracture. The Buccaneers and Panthers submitted their list of inactives at 11:32 a.m. ET on Sunday, 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff of their Week Seven meeting at Bank of America Stadium. After elevating linebacker Caden Fordham from the practice squad, the Buccaneers had 54 available players and thus had to name six inactives to get down to the game-day limit of 48. The Panthers also elevated outside linebacker Nick Hampton and cornerback Robert Rochell from the practice squad and had to name seven inactive players. Carolina will be without one of its top pass-rushers as Jaelan Phillips is out due to a hamstring strain. Fellow outside linebacker Thomas Incoom is also unavailable due to a calf issue, and he was placed on injured reserve on Saturday. away.headline: Panthers' concerns going into Thursday's game against the Packers just got even worse based on the final Week 8 injury report
away.blurb: The Carolina Panthers had a lot of concerns going into this week after the beatdown the team suffered on Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. To make things even harder, the Panthers had a short turnaround to make adjustments with a road trip coming up on Thursday against the Green Bay Packers. That already was going to be a rough road matchup for this team with everything going on coming out of the last game, and to make things even worse, the team's final Week 8 injury report added even more concerns. First off, the Panthers have officially ruled out star pass rusher Jaelan Phillips for the second consecutive game with a hamstring injury. Given the nature of the injury, the fact it's a reaggravation, and this being a short week, it was always unlikely that Phillips would have been able to play against the Packers. Wednesday's injury report confirmed those suspicions, leaving the Panthers without their top edge rusher. Being without Phillips really hurt the Panthers last week. Tampa Bay exposed the Panthers in the run game attacking the edges with counters and rumbled for over 250 yards on the ground. It was an embarrassing performance and not having Phillips out there to set the edge was a big reason for it, along with poor tackling. Big picture, sitting Phillips is the right call for him. He needs to get that hamstring figured out before rushing back into action like he did in Week 6 against the Philadelphia Eagles, which is what caused this injury to reaggravate in the first place. The Panthers need Phillips for the long haul and need him fully healthy before returning. Another notable injury designation is left guard Damien Lewis, who will be out for Thursday's game due to a knee injury. Lewis was easily the team's best offensive lineman, allowing seven pressures this season on over 200 pass blocking snaps. The other four starters have each allowed 15+ pressures this season. The Panthers are also without backup guard Torricelli Simpkins (ankle) and elevated Jake Curhan from the practice squad as a result. The Panthers also placed veteran right tackle Taylor Moton on the injured reserve earlier this week after he fractured his fibula along with further damage to his ankle. That leaves Monroe Freeling to fill back in at right tackle, which in turn forces Rasheed Walker to remain at left tackle. Those two have allowed a combined five sacks and 42 pressures. In Lewis place at left guard, the Panthers will likely turn to Corey Bullock, who's played 71 pass blocking snaps this season with one sack and five pressures allowed. It's a tough look for quarterback Bryce Young, who has been having to overcome pressure all season long. One more worrisome injury to note is in the secondary. Akayleb Evans will not play either due to a triceps/knee injury. Evans has been filling in as a starter, and largely has struggled, in place of Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson. Jackson and Josh Allen are scheduled to duel in a marquee matchup between the Baltimore Ravens and Buffalo Bills . It is a massive spot for a Ravens team that just suffered back-to-back losses in its quarterback's absence and one that could prove whether or not Jesse Minter's squad is a legitimate playoff contender. Closing out the week is another clash of postseason hopefuls in the Seattle Seahawks and Chicago Bears . Both teams won in primetime last week with their Sunday night and Thursday night triumphs, respectively. Only one of them can add another victory when the nation's eyes are trained directly on them on "Monday Night Football." Meanwhile, Buffalo enters fresh off a bye week following road wins at the Rams and Raiders . The Bills have won 4 of the last 5 meetings, including two in the playoffs. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images And then, there was one. The Minnesota Vikings are the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, as the San Francisco 49ers were handed their first loss by the Atlanta Falcons , while the Kansas City Chiefs took their first "L" to the Seattle Seahawks . The Vikings have a massive matchup this week, as they take on the high-flying Lions in Detroit. Elsewhere around the NFL , Lamar Jackson looks to make his return to the field against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills , the Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers face off for the second time in the last month, and the Chicago Bears travel out west to play Sam Darnold and the Seahawks. Which teams should you pick in Week 8, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 27 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Credit to CBS Sports Research Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) (TNF) Dajani ( Packers -3.5): I'm willing to overlook the Carolina Panthers ' surprising 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . They are a better team than what they showed last Sunday, but it's difficult to overlook the fact that Carolina's rushing defense ranks dead last in the NFL with 153.2 yards allowed per game. Josh Jacobs rushed for just 36 yards on 11 carries last week against the Lions in his 2026 debut, but I think he's in for a massive homecoming in primetime on a short week. I'm not saying the Packers run away with this one, but I'll take them to cover 3.5 points. … Prediction: Packers 27, Panthers 23 Dubin (Packers -3.5): It was surprising to see the Panthers get smacked in the face by the Buccaneers last week. The Packers probably can't do the same thing the Bucs did — run the ball down Carolina's throat — but they can still beat that defense with explosive plays. With the top two cornerbacks still out, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden (if he plays) are going to be able to find space in the defense. Green Bay's own defense has also played better of late after a rough start to the season. … Prediction: Packers 24, Panthers 17 Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Dajani ( Ravens +3.5): Ignore that Baltimore allowed 35 unanswered points to the Cincinnati Bengals last week, because it appears that Lamar Jackson is back! He was playing some legitimate MVP-level ball before getting hurt, as Jackson went 3-1 as the starter, while completing 70.8% of his passes with 10.1 yards per attempt, six passing touchdowns and just one interception. Only four quarterbacks have put up those kinds of numbers in their first four starts of a season in the past 40 years. The Ravens are a completely different team with Jackson under center, and this Bills defense allows too many points. Buffalo ranks third-worst in scoring defense (28.5 ppg), and has allowed at least 30 points in four of its five victories this season. Jackson is 10-5 SU and 13-2 ATS as an underdog in his career. He's statistically the best quarterback to bet on when listed as an underdog since 1970. … Prediction: Ravens 30, Bills 28 Dubin (Ravens +3.5): This is the same deal as with the Ravens and me pretty much every week: flip the pick if Lamar Jackson sits out again. Otherwise, I like the Ravens to at least keep things close against the Bills. Both of these offenses have been pretty excellent, and the Ravens have been especially so when Jackson has been on the field with Zay Flowers . Ultimately, though, the Bills' home-field advantage and the weaknesses in Baltimore's own pass defense lead me to take the Bills to win and the Ravens to cover. … Prediction: Bills 30, Ravens 27 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) Dajani (Lions -3): I'm shocked by this line, honestly. The only remaining undefeated team in the NFL is a three-point underdog to a division rival? With that said, I think I agree with it. The Vikings' defense is the main reason they are 5-0, as they've allowed a league-leading 12.3 points per game, plus registered a league-leading 10.6% sack rate and 47.6% pressure rate. Offensively, the Vikings have the fewest touchdowns (10) by a 6-0 team since the 1934 Lions and rank 31st in offensive EPA. They could have lost last week to the Indianapolis Colts , who are in the midst of a fire sale. As for the Lions, the concern has always been with their defense. But I think Kelvin Sheppard 's unit is coming along. They allowed just 17 points to the Packers last week, and Brian Branch is back in the lineup. Maybe we could see a push here, but I'm taking the Lions to win … Prediction: Lions 24, Vikings 20 Dubin (Lions -3): Detroit has recently been thrown off its offensive game by Brian Flores' defense, but the offense is operating at an extremely high level right now, with Jared Goff playing as well as he has in recent memory. And as Dajani said, this Minnesota offense just does not have the ability to get into a high-scoring game and come away with a win. They need the defense to hold the opponent down entirely, and I'm not sure that even Flores' bunch can do that in the friendly confines of Ford Field. … Prediction: Lions 23, Vikings 14 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) Dajani (Steelers -3.5): How can the Browns keep getting away with this? They overcame a 14-0 deficit in Nashville on Sunday, as Harold Fannin Jr . took a short reception 36 yards down the field with 20 seconds remaining to set up a 32-yard game-winning field goal from Andre Szmyt . Deshaun Watson became the third quarterback since 1970 to register a game-winning drive in each of his team's first five wins of the season. With this being a divisional game against an opponent that just got back from Paris, I can understand why some would take the points with the underdog given the hook. But the Steelers are 3-0 ATS at home. That includes Week 3, when they dropped 30 points on Joe Burrow and the Bengals in a win, and Week 5, when Pittsburgh scored 34 points in a double-digit victory over the Colts. The Steelers are averaging 26.0 points per game over their last five contests, which ranks top 10 in the NFL, and are 8-0 SU and ATS in their last eight home games vs. the Browns. In fact, Pittsburgh is actually a perfect 11-0 ATS in its last 11 home divisional games. Insane stat. … Prediction: Steelers 26, Browns 21 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): I don't understand how the Browns keep doing it. Every single one of their victories has required a game-winning drive in the final five minutes of the game. That's not sustainable on any level whatsoever. The Steelers don't exactly have consistency written all over them, considering the vagaries of their passing game and the fact that their three-game winning streak has come against weak opponents. However, I trust Jaylen Warren and Co. more than I do the Browns at this point. … Prediction: Steelers 20, Browns 13 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) Dajani (Falcons +2.5): I have plenty of questions about both of these teams, but I did tell you the Falcons were going to cover the small number vs. the 49ers last week! Atlanta finished that game on a 26-6 run after trailing 14-3. They scored on four straight drives. I'm not sure the Buccaneers deserve to be three-point favorites this week after that destruction of the Panthers. Baker Mayfield had to throw for just 64 yards and a touchdown in a 43-13 victory, as Bucky Irving , Kenneth Gainwell and Sean Tucker combined for 246 yards rushing and three touchdowns. This Falcons rush defense ranks fourth in the NFL with 88.9 rushing yards allowed per game. Plus, the Falcons have won two road games this season by 20+ points after being listed as an underdog, and are 4-0 ATS in their last four road games against the Buccaneers. … Prediction: Falcons 26, Buccaneers 24 Dubin (Falcons +2.5): The Buccaneers ran all over the Panthers last week, but Atlanta has actually been quite good against the run, allowing only 3.8 yards per carry this season. Can Tampa really control the game with Bucky Irving the way it did last week, or will it have to actually turn Baker Mayfield loose as a passer here? If the Bucs have to do that, I have more confidence in Atlanta's offense right now, with Bijan Robinson , Drake London and even Kyle Pitts contributing at a high level. … Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 17 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Dajani ( Broncos +1.5): The Broncos had an embarrassing outing last time they played the Chiefs, allowing 247 yards off of 28 missed tackles in a 31-10 loss. There has been a lot of talk about Bo Nix and the offense, but what about the Chiefs? They averaged 4.3 yards per play and recorded just 213 yards of total offense in that embarrassing loss to the Seahawks. The team seemingly never got off the bus. Fresh off their bye week, the Bills are looking to pick up where they left off offensively, but hope to find more success on defense. It won't be easy since they will be facing a strong Ravens team, which will be getting a boost thanks to the return of quarterback Lamar Jackson. After missing three games with a high ankle sprain, Jackson is expected to make his way back to the field against the Bills. That means both teams will have their MVP quarterbacks on the field and the last time they met was in Week 1 of the 2025 season. Will: Titans’ secondary sees massive uptick Two weeks in a row now, Tennessee has forced at least one interception. The Titans have come down with three picks over the last two games, two of which belong to rising offseason pickup Cor’Dale Flott. Tennessee Titans cornerback Cor'dale Flott (18) intercepts Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) on Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. The Bengals score a lot - a lot - of points. TeamRankings has Cincinnati fourth in the NFL in points per game (27.2) and touchdowns per game (3.2). Their passing statistics specifically are top 10 across the board regarding pass play percentage, completion percentage, and pass yards per game. Tennessee is facing one of the best pass-first teams in the NFL. If Saleh's secondary can find consistency beyond the occasional turnover, the Titans would have more than a fair chance to shut down RB Chase Brown on the ground, too. It's much easier to stop Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins in concept than it is on the field, but doing so is the Titans' key to winning this one. Won’t: Titans can't overcome inconsistent Bengals defense The inverse, of course, is if the Titans' offense continues to suffer. The Bengals have proved themselves beatable against "bad" teams - just see their narrow, one-score win over the 1-6 Miami Dolphins two weeks ago. But Cincinnati also just dismantled the Baltimore Ravens last week, 35-13. The through line is that Cincy scored 30+ points in both of those contests; it comes down to the opposing offense's ability to hang in there when Burrow and his crew get hot. Tennessee ranks 31st in both touchdowns and points per game. Almost everywhere the Bengals are in the top 10 through the air, the Titans are in the bottom 10. Cincy has allowed 20+ points in four of their six games this season. If Cam Ward can get back on his feet in any sense of the saying, another 24-point performance like Tennessee had last week could be enough to at least make this one interesting. However, the Titans may need a little more juice than they've seen yet this season from their QB to stay in it. Prediction: Titans lose, 31-20 Ultimately, I have the Titans falling to 1-7 in this one. We've seen a number of trends solidify that this roster has failed to prove their ability to rise beyond. Carnell Tate is the primary receiver in an otherwise underwhelming offense. The defense can force early turnovers, but can't get late stops when it matters - especially when it comes to tackling. Ward has a better second half than his typically abysmal first, but by the time Tennessee tries to get aggressive, it's too late to make a difference. I expect most of, if not all of these notes to be hit in Week 8. I don't think the Titans will lose in a blowout, but on the road against one of the best offenses in the league, this one already looks like too much for Saleh's team. Simmons was the shining star and identity of the Tennessee Titans defense. His absence up front will drop the Titans even further down the defensive pecking order, which says something when they're already dead last in DVOA at FTN . The Bengals picked apart a very good Ravens stop unit in the second half of last week's win. Titans vs Bengals combo The Bengals do the lion's share of the scoring, but don't discount the Titans. They're playing with pace and face a Bengals defense that still has work to do. He faces a watered-down Titans defense that's allowed six scores to running backs. Tee Higgins ' projections call for as many as 91 yards against a Titans secondary giving up explosive plays. He no longer has to worry about one of the premier run stoppers in the game, facing a Titans red-zone defense now missing its biggest cog. Even when Simmons was in the mix, the Titans had allowed six scores to rival RBs. Brown has only one touchdown in 2026 despite 13 carries and three receptions in the red zone. That includes a 44-yard dinger on a broken play with Burrow dodging pressure. We mentioned the Titans' problems giving up home runs over the top, and Higgins is one of the best deep threats in the land, averaging 21.6 air yards per reception and amassing eight catches for 20+ yards. The Titans have also been burned by WR2s to start the season, ranking 24th in DVOA vs. WR2s at FTN while giving up almost 56 yards per game to those second options. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. ET from Paycor Stadium in Cincinnati, Ohio. The game will broadcast live on CBS. The Bengals are 12.5-point favorites over the Titans on the spread, with the total set at over/under 45.5 points. Cincinnati is a -850 moneyline favorite to win outright, while Tennessee is a +590 underdog to pull off the upset. Let's get into my Titans vs Bengals predictions and NFL picks for Sunday, November 1. Titans vs Bengals Odds for NFL Week 8 Titans vs Bengals spread : Titans +12.5 (-105), Titans -12.5 (-115) Titans vs Bengals total : over/under 45.5 (-115o / 105u) Titans vs Bengals moneyline : Titans +590, Bengals -850 Tennessee Titans vs Cincinnati Bengals Betting Preview Titans Betting Preview: Life Without Jeffery Simmons Fading the Titans has been a profitable endeavor this year, but they have covered the number in each of their last two road games. I provided the breakdown for their victory on the road in Indianapolis and their road cover as 11-point underdogs in Baltimore back in Week 4. I will not be going back to the well for a third time in this spot against the Bengals as too many factors are working against them. For starters, the Titans traded away their best defensive player this week in Jeffery Simmons and will also be without leading receiver in Carnell Tate. Opposing running backs have averaged four yards per carry against Tennessee with Simmons on the field — that number increases to 4.5 yards per carry on the 35 carries he has not been in the lineup. The Titans' explosive rush rate allowed also increases from 9.8% with Simmons to 14.3% without Simmons on the field. Simmons boasts the fifth-highest pass rush grade this season out of all defensive tackles , per Pro Football Focus. The lack of interior pressure will allow Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow to build upon his red-hot finish to Week 7. Burrow was surgical in the second half versus Baltimore, completing 88% of his passes for an average of 13.8 yards per attempt. Burrow is heating up, as he historically does as the season progresses — and now, he gets a highly exploitable matchup. Tennessee's defense under head coach Robert Saleh ranks 31st in completion percentage allowed and 27th in yards per attempt allowed. The Titans' pressure rate of 30.6% ranks 26th. However, it is even more concerning when looking at the time charted to get those pressures on quarterbacks. The Titans' 2.8 seconds per pressure is the worst in the NFL, and that number is almost certainly going to get worse with the loss of Simmons. If Tennessee is going to make this game competitive, it has to be the doing of Cam Ward. Tony Pollard and the running game were excellent a week ago versus Cleveland, but the Bengals have the most improved run defense in the league. Bengals Betting Preview: Good Spot for Cincy's Defense Al Golden's defense plays with the highest rate of light boxes in alignment, yet still leads the NFL in stuff rate defending running games. Golden can opt to add an extra defender on early downs to stymie Pollard, which will force Ward into long down-and-distance situations. Without their top weapon on the outside in Tate, the Titans lack playmakers to move the chains when they get to third down. Ward and company already struggle in these situations, ranking 27th in third-down conversion rate. The Bengals boast the eighth-best defense per dropback, according to expected points added (EPA). Projecting the Titans' success in this spot becomes extremely difficult when you consider that 43% of all their pass attempts on 2nd-and-8+ and 28% of all attempts on 3rd- or 4th-and-8+ longer were funneled to Tate. The Titans' passing game is facing an uphill battle in overcoming their deficiencies when their running game on standard downs isn't keeping them ahead of schedule. Titans vs Bengals Best Bets, Analysis Tennessee has a -62 scoring margin in the first half of games this season, which is the worst in the league. The Titans will likely fall behind early and have no choice but to abandon the running game. This further puts the onus of any potential comeback in the hands of Cam Ward. Ward's 27.1 passer rating under pressure and turnover-worthy throw rate nearly doubling his big-time throw rate makes it too difficult to trust him in delivering any chance at a backdoor cover. The Bengals are -6.5 in the 1st half, which is another position worth a look. However, I am more comfortable allowing the full 60 minutes to play out as Ward's game-altering mistake(s) can come at any time. Joe Burrow is heating up at the right time and the Titans do not have the personnel to slow him down. I expect the Bengals to cruise to victory with significant margin. home.headline: Injury Report: Week 8 vs Cowboys
home.blurb: The Cardinals had been cautious with the rookie running back, but after three practices, the coaching staff felt Love was healthy enough to return. "Even though he's he's been out for two weeks, none of these guys by November 1st are truly at 100 (percent)," coach Mike LaFleur said. "But he's feeling as good as he can feel you know so yeah kind of go from there." Who will be blocking for him might be the bigger question. Center Hjalte Froholdt is questionable to play after being limited on Thursday with a knee injury. He did not practice on Friday. If unable to play, Hayden Conner could slide to center and the Cardinals would start a different player at right guard for the fourth time this season. Defensively, some reinforcements could be on the way. After missing the last three weeks, safety Dewey Wingard (knee) logged a full week of practice. He is questionable to play, as is cornerback Max Melton after he missed last weekend with a knee issue. Dallas ruled out wide receiver KaVontae Turpin (ribs) and linebacker Dee Winters (calf). Six players are questionable to play including defensive tackle Kenny Clark (back) and wide receiver George Pickens (shoulder/hamstring). Wide receiver Michael Wilson (ribs) wore the yellow non-contact pinny for a second consecutive day. He told the media on Wednesday it is out of caution. Wilson was one of eight players limited for practice. Center Hjalte Froholdt appeared on the injury report and was limited with a knee injury. His status this weekend will be important to monitor since backup center Hayden Conner is currently playing right guard. The Cowboys were back at practice on Thursday. They opened up the 21-day practice window for defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard. Safety Caleb Downs (ankle), wide receiver George Pickens (shoulder/hamstring), and defensive tackle Quinnen Williams (hamstring) were limited. Wide receiver Michael Wilson was wearing a yellow non-contact jersey. He appeared on the injury report with a ribs issue. He was limited. Multiple players returned to practice after being inactive on Sunday. Jeremiyah Love (ankle), safety Dewey Wingard (knee), cornerback Max Melton (knee), and quarterback Carson Beck (back) were limited. Cornerback Kei'Trel Clark was limited with an illness. Since the Cowboys did not practice on Wednesday, the designations were estimations. Wide receiver George Pickens was limited and listed with a shoulder and hamstring issue. The Vikings, which have yet to lose a game this season (6-0), are coming off a 16-10 win over the Indianapolis Colts. Meanwhile, Detroit defeated Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers a week ago, 20-17. Without further ado, here are the predictions from the Detroit Lions On SI staff for the Lions' Week 8 matchup with Minnesota. Christian Booher The Lions have a chance to truly solidify themselves as division title contenders with a win over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday. Though the Vikings have underwhelmed offensively at times, they have found a way to start the season 6-0, thanks in part to a dominant defense that will be the best unit Detroit has faced to date. As a result, the pressure will be on Detroit's offense to come up with answers for a group that is led by one of the best defensive minds in football in Vikings coordinator Brian Flores. Jared Goff holds the key, as if he can get the ball out quickly and find answers within the opposition he will have a good chance to lead his group to a dominant performance. It's also an opportunity for the Lions' defense to make a statement against Kyler Murray. I think this game will feature turnovers on both sides, with the unit that gets the ball last ultimately finding a way to win. Detroit gets that advantage, as Goff leads Detroit to a game-winning field goal and a statement division victory. The Lions find a way to win ugly, and remind the league that they are capable of making a playoff run. Lions 23, Vikings 20 The Detroit Lions will face arguably their toughest test of the season yet when they square off with the undefeated Minnesota Vikings Sunday. The Vikings’ defense has been the definition of elite this season, allowing a measly 12.3 points per game (No. 1 in the NFL). You combine that with a stingy pass defense, and Lions signal-caller Jared Goff should have his hands full in the Week 8 affair. Plus, Detroit's defensive back and linebacker groups will need to bring their “A game” against Minnesota pass-catchers Justin Jefferson and T.J. Hockenson. It won't be easy for the Lions to emerge victorious in this divisional contest. However, I believe they will on the heels of strong efforts from their pass-rush and star running back Jahmyr Gibbs. I believe that Gibbs will help seal the deal for Detroit with several key runs in the fourth quarter, ultimately setting up Jake Bates for the game-winning kick. Lions 24, Vikings 21 John Maakaron This is a game the Lions would ideally like to get out to an early lead, as the Vikings offense is far behind the defense. Brian Flores is sure to bring the pressure from a variety of different spots, but Jared Goff should be able to make good decisions and distribute the football to Detroit’s skill position players. The most interesting matchup may end up being the Vikings offense against Detroit’s defense, given that both units are the clear weaknesses of their respective teams. Expect Jahmyr Gibbs to be responsible for another heavy workload at Ford Field. Lions 23, Vikings 17 Emmett Matasovsky The Lions take on the undefeated Minnesota Vikings in a headline matchup for Week 8. Overall, I see this being a slightly higher-scoring matchup than last week’s divisional showdown between the Packers and Lions. The Vikings defense is not exactly stout, ranking 23rd in the league in total defense. Combine that with Detroit having a series of unforced errors while breaking Cade Mays into game action at center, and it is hard to see the Lions not outscoring their 20 points last week. Kyler Murray is a mobile quarterback, and that has been a trend of a noticeable struggle for Detroit defenses. That said, the Vikings’ offensive greatness in their first six games also has come against the second-easiest schedule in the league. I see Detroit giving the Vikings the first mark in the latter’s loss column, with Jared Goff making several key plays. The Vikings, which have yet to lose a game this season (6-0), feature both a bottom-10 offense (20.8 points/game) and the league's top defensive unit. Coordinated by Brian Flores, Minnesota's defense has permitted just 12.3 points a game, and hasn't allowed more than 16 points in a game since Week 2. And most recently, the Vikings surrendered just 10 points in a 16-10 victory over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 7. Additionally, Minnesota has been extremely stout against the pass thus far this season. In fact, Kevin O'Connell's squad has allowed the second-fewest passing yards (930) and the least amount of touchdowns through the air (three) through the season's first seven weeks. The Vikings have also already secured seven interceptions, spearheaded by cornerback Byron Murphy's league-high three picks. So, Lions signal-caller Jared Goff, who has yet to throw an interception in 2026, will face arguably his biggest test of the campaign against Minnesota's stingy pass defense . Then on the opposite side of the ball, Detroit's secondary will receive one of its toughest assignments of the year, going head-to-head with All-Pro wideout Justin Jefferson. Jefferson, who has surpassed 1,000 receiving yards in each of his first six NFL seasons, has accumulated 302 reception yards and three touchdowns in five games this season. He's unquestionably Vikings passer Kyler Murray's go-to target and one of the very best receivers in the game today. Subsequently, D.J. Reed, the Lions’ No. 1 cornerback , should get the majority of one-on-one reps with the Pro Bowl pass-catcher. Additionally, I wouldn't be surprised if Detroit defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard deployed a rotation of corners in the Week 8 tilt. And as a result, I could see the likes of Ennis Rakestraw and Roger McCreary also getting opportunities to defend Jefferson Sunday. It'll hardly be an easy task for the Lions’ defensive backs group. However, Detroit does have a solid track record against Jefferson, having limited him to under 60 yards the past three meetings between the NFC North rivals . And if the Lions could do it a fourth straight time, it would go a long way toward Dan Campbell's squad notching its fifth victory on the season. At this present juncture, I'm willing to give Detroit a 61 percent chance to secure the Week 8 victory . away.blurb: Vikings Final Injury Report vs Lions: Only One Player Questionable - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Vikings Final Injury Report vs Lions: Only One Player Questionable Running back Aaron Jones and left guard Joe Huber both sat out Wednesday with knee injuries. Right tackle Brian O'Neill was limited with the same listed "knee" ailment. On Thursday, tight end Gavin Bartholomew was added to the list of non-participants. Vikings at full health… except Jay Ward is suddenly questionable Fortunately, by Friday, all four were full participants, and none of them received a game status on the final injury report . That doesn't mean the Vikings got through the week clean, though. One new name popped up on the report Friday. Jay Ward is suddenly questionable for Sunday in Detroit. After a rollercoaster week on the Vikings injury report, safety Jay Ward (Questionable) is the only player who goes into Week 8 with a designation pic.twitter.com/RW3IAQyv0b Ward, a fourth-year safety out of LSU, has mostly been a special teams player this season. He has played 110 special teams snaps (69%) and just four defensive snaps through six games, with six tackles. Last year, he started five games and played 248 defensive snaps. Harrison Smith (limited) and Christian Darrisaw (did not practice) also showed up on Friday's report, but both were veteran rest days, and neither got a designation. Jones went from not practicing Wednesday to limited Thursday to full Friday. He has played through a sprained MCL since Week 2 and aggravated it in Sunday's win over the Indianapolis Colts. away.headline: Breaking Down Vikings' Injury Report for Week 8 After Win Over the Colts (Who's Hurt and Who Could Return)
away.blurb: Breaking Down Vikings' Injury Report for Week 8 After Win Over the Colts (Who's Hurt and Who Could Return) Skip to main content SI.COM Minnesota moved to 6-0 after getting past the listless Colts, and also came out of the game relatively healthy as an added bonus. A few Vikings did leave the game with injury, though, so there are a few names to watch this week ahead of a date with the Detroit Lions. Vikings who could return in Week 8 Price took a big hit on a punt return and was evaluated for a concussion. He was cleared to return to the game, but head coach Kevin O'Connell did say that Price was dealing with a stinger after the win. It didn't seem to affect the star returner, and there shouldn't be much concern heading into Week 8. Still, Price is one of those players that is darn-near irreplaceable for the Vikings if he did have to miss time. The Vikings' first-round pick exited the game with an apparent lower-body injury. And while his name didn't come up postgame as a possible serious injury, Banks' two previous foot injuries that forced him out of football for almost a year are certainly at the forefront of fans' minds. Banks didn't return after limping off the field , and his status will be something to monitor throughout the week. Luckily, the Vikings didn't appear to lose anyone to a long-term injury on Sunday. The key Vikings out for the season remained the same with Donovan Jackson, Josh Oliver, Jamal Adams and Tyler Batty all already lost for the year. With various injuries on offense, defense and even one on special teams, here's who should be fine, and who might miss some time for Minnesota. Like Price, Addison was evaluated for a concussion before being cleared to play shortly after. Still, he wasn't able to do much in the contest, notching just two catches for 20 yards. Addison had already missed the Week 5 contest with a hamstring issue, but it appears he should have a clean bill of health to try and right the ship heading into the Lions matchup. Jones has been battling a knee injury all season, and once again aggravated it late in the game against the Colts. O'Connell called the injury day-to-day after the game, but it wouldn't be too surprising if Jones needs a week off to let things heal. The Vikings have ridden Jones hard this season with Jordan Mason's own injury issues, and the toll on his body is adding up quickly. If Jones can't shake this nagging knee issue, the Vikings could look to make a move for another runner at the trade deadline . Still, Jones has given his all this season, and it's hard to see him voluntarily coming off the field. Obviously injury concerns have been a big talking point with Banks, and if he does have to miss time, fellow rookie Domonique Orange could get some more run . away.headline: Vikings-Lions Final Injury Report
away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Lions, Kerby Joseph had his three-week window opened to return from IR this week but will not return this week. Starting slot cornerback Roger McCreary was a late addition to the Lions’ injury report on Friday, when he was limited with a foot injury. He is questionable for Sunday’s game, which means he’s likely to play. For the Vikings, close to a clean sheet with just a late addition of Jay Ward to the injury report on Friday with knee issue. He was limited on Friday and listed as questionable, but again that means he’s likely to play. So, looks like full rosters will be available for both teams on Sunday, except for those on IR. home.blurb: Vikings Final Injury Report vs Lions: Only One Player Questionable - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Vikings Final Injury Report vs Lions: Only One Player Questionable Running back Aaron Jones and left guard Joe Huber both sat out Wednesday with knee injuries. Right tackle Brian O'Neill was limited with the same listed "knee" ailment. On Thursday, tight end Gavin Bartholomew was added to the list of non-participants. Vikings at full health… except Jay Ward is suddenly questionable Fortunately, by Friday, all four were full participants, and none of them received a game status on the final injury report . That doesn't mean the Vikings got through the week clean, though. One new name popped up on the report Friday. Jay Ward is suddenly questionable for Sunday in Detroit. After a rollercoaster week on the Vikings injury report, safety Jay Ward (Questionable) is the only player who goes into Week 8 with a designation pic.twitter.com/RW3IAQyv0b Ward, a fourth-year safety out of LSU, has mostly been a special teams player this season. He has played 110 special teams snaps (69%) and just four defensive snaps through six games, with six tackles. Last year, he started five games and played 248 defensive snaps. Harrison Smith (limited) and Christian Darrisaw (did not practice) also showed up on Friday's report, but both were veteran rest days, and neither got a designation. Jones went from not practicing Wednesday to limited Thursday to full Friday. He has played through a sprained MCL since Week 2 and aggravated it in Sunday's win over the Indianapolis Colts. home.headline: Vikings-Lions Final Injury Report
home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Lions, Kerby Joseph had his three-week window opened to return from IR this week but will not return this week. Starting slot cornerback Roger McCreary was a late addition to the Lions’ injury report on Friday, when he was limited with a foot injury. He is questionable for Sunday’s game, which means he’s likely to play. For the Vikings, close to a clean sheet with just a late addition of Jay Ward to the injury report on Friday with knee issue. He was limited on Friday and listed as questionable, but again that means he’s likely to play. So, looks like full rosters will be available for both teams on Sunday, except for those on IR. home.blurb: When looking at this injury report, the biggest takeaway is the fact that the Vikings do not have any players out for this game which is a good sign, especially because the season is now in Week 8 and the hits have begun to add up, but even so Minnesota has been able to stay mostly healthy. Now looking at the players on this injury report, Ward is questionable and it is unknown whether or not he will play on Sunday. So, it will be interesting to see if he is active or if he does end up being out which could require someone to step up as Ward is a backup safety and a solid special teams contributor. With that said, it will be interesting to see if Ward plays in this game and if someone has to step up in his place, as well as if this offense can figure out a way to get going, because if they can, they may have a great chance to improve to 7-0 and remain the only undefeated team in the NFL . Game picks for Raiders Week 8 matchup vs Jets Lance Fernandez -- Jets 24, Raiders 20 The Jets have struggled offensively, ranking in the bottom half in passing yards, rushing yards, and points per game. Jets 17 The Raiders will have some success running the ball and getting pressure on Geno Smith. Look for Brock Bowers and Tre Tucker to have good games. The Browns are no easy challenge this time around, and the Steelers learned that firsthand several weeks ago. The Browns won their first meeting on Thursday Night Football, but the matchup shifts to Acrisure Stadium for Week 8, and the Steelers intend to exact some revenge on their divisional foes. Both squads enter with a 5-2 record and a share of the AFC North lead. It’s a measuring-stick showdown between the Steelers and Browns, and bold actions will be taken. Both Teams Score 25 Points or More Both of these franchises bring strong defenses to their Week 8 contest. The Steelers rank in the top 10 in total yards allowed per game, rushing yards allowed per game and points allowed per contest. They also rank 11th in passing yards allowed per game. Similarly, the Browns rank in the top 15 across multiple defensive categories. It’s going to be a matchup of two stout defensive units, right? Well what would be more surprising than these two teams putting up an offensive showdown? That’s what could be in store for these two teams, despite all signs pointing toward the opposite. The Steelers rank 22nd in the NFL in points per game, posting an average of 21.9. The Browns trail, recording the 28th-best average of 19.0 points per game. But, the Steelers have also reached the 24-point mark four times in seven tries, and they could put up even more in Week 8. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Aaron Rodgers Hits 300 Yards for First Time With Steelers Aaron Rodgers Hits 300 Yards for First Time With Steelers If the Steelers are going to buck the trend and put up points, there are two approaches to help accomplish that. One is to exploit their 19th-ranked run defense, which has to be at the top of their game plan as Jaylen Warren continues to put up MVP-caliber production. Another avenue, the more unexpected one for the offense to take, is to push the ball downfield with the passing game. In the team’s first matchup against the Browns, Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf posted five receptions on nine targets for 115 yards. And they managed to break off his biggest play of the game by getting him away from Cleveland’s top defender, Denzel Ward. If the Steelers can capture that again in Week 8, quarterback Aaron Rodgers could have a magical day. In 2025, Rodgers never hit the 300-yard mark. His 2026 season high so far is 299 yards, which he threw for during that previous contest against the Browns. In the three weeks since, he hasn’t surpassed 255 yards, but this could be the one where he eclipses 300 yards. Germie 100-Yard Game Incoming If Rodgers is throwing that many yards, one of his receivers has to have an outstanding day on the stat sheet. After he earned more and more trust, Bernard could face a favorable matchup if he doesn’t go against Ward too often. He’s gotten close, putting up two 80+ yard games so far this season. This week, it finally happens. The second-round pick eclipses 100 yards for the first time in his young NFL career. picks.blurb: NFL predictions: Steelers will ride offense to win over Browns - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL Week 8 updates CFB winners & losers Week 8 Fantasy Football Toolkit Williams earns MVP honors Alvarez schools Mbilli NFL predictions: Steelers will ride offense to win over Browns (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Joey Bray Sat, October 31, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The one game standing between the 5-2 Pittsburgh Steelers and their bye week is their most consequential yet, as they are set to take on the 5-2 Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh. When the ball is kicked, it will be exactly a month to the day since Cleveland took the first game between the teams on Thursday Night Football. However, the Steelers have rattled off three straight wins since then. The winner of this game will be in sole possession of first place in the AFC North heading into the second half of the regular season. With both teams coming off wins and identical records, FanDuel Sportsbook gives the Pittsburgh Steelers the slight edge as a 3.5-point favorite over Cleveland. This is as close to a "must-win" game in the middle of the season for the Steelers as we will ever see. With all of that being said, here are some predictions based around my favorite prop bets of the weekend. Germie Bernard over 43.5 receiving yards TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 18: Wide receiver Germie Bernard #17 of the Pittsburgh Steelers celebrates the first down in the fourth quarter at Raymond James Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images) | Getty Images This number is ridiculously low because the rookie receiver will be one of, if not the most targeted pass catchers on the entire team on Sunday. Last time these two teams met, Bernard got barely any playing time, but that gives him the chance to take advantage of a group that hasn't seen what he can do yet. In their first matchup, Pittsburgh had two receivers go over this total. I'm not letting last game scare me, as the Steelers controlled the clock running the football, leading to limited opportunities for any receiver. It would be a shock to see no receiver have more than three catches for the second week in a row. Bernard is a volume receiver that the Steelers will need to rely on to get open and break some tackles against their tough man defense. Rico Dowdle gets over 70 scrimmage yards TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 18: Ifeatu Melifonwu #5 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers tackles Rico Dowdle #13 of the Pittsburgh Steelers during the first half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ever since running back Rico Dowdle has returned to the lineup from his toe injury, he has looked significantly more efficient with the ball in his hands. Sure, the improved offensive line helps, but Dowdle is going to continue to earn more runs in the offense with his numbers improving. Last week, the veteran back averaged a season-high 4.6 yards per carry. Dowdle also hauled in six passes, good for the most on the team, for 45 yards. It was a more even share of the opportunities for the Steelers running backs, as Dowdle had 16 touches compared to Jaylen Warren's 21. Dowdle is the change of pace back in the Steelers offense, but is one that they will continue to use quite a bit as he gets healthier. Warren's breakout doesn't mean that Dowdle won't be involved in the offense. In fact, I think what we saw against New Orleans is what we can expect from Dowdle for the rest of the season. With the browns struggles to defend the run, both backs could be in for a big day on Sunday. Darnell Washington continues dominance with a touchdown TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 18: Darnell Washington #80 of the Pittsburgh Steelers scores a touchdown against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on a pass from Aaron Rodgers #8 during the second half of the game at Raymond James Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Steelers' six-foot-seven tight end has already set career highs in total touchdowns this season. His increased usage in the red zone is something Steelers fans have been begging to see for years now. Last week, Washington dunked on Saints defensive back Kool-Aid McKinstry as he snatched the ball out of the air from four yards out for the Steelers' only touchdown in Paris. The tight end has caught a touchdown pass in two consecutive games, and I have a hard time seeing that trend stopping against Cleveland given his continued usage in the red zone. Washington also scored against the Browns in their first matchup a month ago. It almost makes too much sense to see Washington in the end zone again on Sunday. picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Browns: 4 bold predictions for this week's game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL Week 8 updates CFB winners & losers Week 8 Fantasy Football Toolkit Williams earns MVP honors Alvarez schools Mbilli Steelers vs. Browns: 4 bold predictions for this week's game Curt Popejoy, Steelers Wire Sat, October 31, 2026 at 6:36 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cleveland Browns square off, both teams at 5-2 and tied on top in the AFC North. The Steelers are looking for payback and the Browns are looking for their first sweep of the Steelers since 1988. Here are four bold predictions for this week's game. Jaylen Warren carries the offense The Browns run defense is struggling and Jaylen Warren is on a tear. Warren rushed for 93 yards in the first matchup and our bold prediction for Warren this week is he gets his fourth 100-yard rushing game of the year and tops 150 yards of total offense and two total touchdowns. T.J. Watt breaks out with 3 sacks This week is the perfect opportunity for T.J. Watt to quiet the critics as he faces backup right tackle Dawand Jones. Watt is currently fourth int he NFL with 5.5 sacks but has struggled with consistent pressure. This week he breaks out of his funk with a huge three-sack performance and one of them turns into a huge forced fumble. Pittsburgh solves their red zone woes with two scores For all the things he can do, head coach Mike McCarthy has struggled to get the Steelers red-zone offense on track. This is due in large part because he's been unwilling to just run the football near the goal line. That ends this week with two short rushing touchdowns. The Steelers currently have only one rushing touchdown all season. Double-digit win for the Steelers We appreciate what the Browns are building but Pittsburgh is at home and riding a three-game win streak since the loss to Cleveland and will keep it going with a double-digit win, bringing the Browns back to Earth about their place in the AFC North.
