away.blurb: 3 Browns are questionable as team works out five players ahead of Week 8 According to ESPN’s Daniel Oyefusi , the Browns worked out five players ahead of the weekend: tackle Blake Austin, guard C.J. Hanson, center Jacob Rizy, and wide receivers Xavier Weaver and Brady Boyd. Head coach Todd Monken did not rule Howard out, however. He was listed as questionable for Week 8 along with defensive back Myles Harden and safety Daniel Thomas. 2 ruled out, 1 questionable for Steelers who enter this game close to full health The Steelers are healthy as well. They ruled out a pair of depth defensive backs in Brandin Echols and Doneiko Slaughter on Friday. Both players have mostly played on special teams for Pittsburgh. Wide receiver Ben Skowronek is questionable for Sunday with a calf injury. He’s only been targeted four times by Aaron Rodgers in five game appearances this season. Can the Browns figure out how to score in the first quarter? The Steelers enter this game allowing 4.3 points per game in the first quarter. They should be able to put the Browns’ most maddening trend to the test out of the gate. Cleveland played man-to-man on Pittsburgh’s receivers on over 70% of Rodgers’ dropbacks in Week 4. The Steelers’ inability to create quick separation, and Rodgers’ propensity to get the ball out quickly, led to a 55% completion percentage and a lot of failed drives. The Browns are becoming a bad matchup for the Steelers, and that’s why we have them grinding out another close win. Watson has been getting the ball out quicker and making sounder decisions. Cleveland has the personnel, like tight end Harold Fannin, wide receiver KC Concepcion, and running back Dylan Sampson, to turn quick passes into big gains, limiting Pittsburgh’s elite pass rush. This game could easily go the Steelers’ way if the Browns struggle with sacks and turnovers. But if they can protect the football and get it out quickly, they should be in position to win it in the fourth quarter. Week 8 is dripping with opportunity for the Cleveland Browns. This is the spot, playing in a stadium that’s been a house of horrors for decades, that turns a feel-good start to the season into something much more real. The Browns are as healthy as they’ve been all season and are playing their best football, at least in terms of stringing together all three phases. A win over Pittsburgh would clinch their first regular-season sweep in the rivalry since the 1980s and would vault their record to 6-2 atop the AFC North. Browns fans have been craving meaningful football. It doesn’t get much bigger than Sunday’s trip to Pittsburgh. picks.headline: FalconsSI Staff Split on Falcons vs. Buccaneers Week 8 Predictions
picks.blurb: FalconsSI Staff Split on Falcons vs. Buccaneers Week 8 Predictions Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Atlanta Falcons have an opportunity to make a major statement in Week 8 when they travel to face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. Coming off an impressive victory over the previously undefeated San Francisco 49ers, Atlanta has a chance to carry that momentum into a divisional matchup with significant NFC South implications. The Buccaneers are coming off a blowout victory over the Carolina Panthers, but their 2-5 record leaves them needing a win to keep their divisional hopes alive. Meanwhile, a Falcons victory would give Atlanta sole possession of first place in the NFC South. Here is how the FalconsSI staff sees Sunday’s matchup playing out. Scott Kennedy (3-4) This is the ultimate Lucy and Charlie Brown game for Falcons fans. Atlanta is coming off an impressive home victory against the San Francisco 49ers, while Tampa Bay remains just 2-5 despite a blowout win over Carolina. The opportunity is there for the Falcons to take sole possession of first place in the NFC South and potentially put the Buccaneers’ divisional hopes on life support. This is exactly the kind of game Atlanta should win. Unfortunately, it is also the type of game the Falcons have dropped year after frustrating year. However, looking beyond the history of disappointment, Atlanta is playing better football than Tampa Bay right now. The Falcons and Buccaneers can both run and stop the run, but Atlanta is getting better quarterback play and has a better set of (healthy) weapons on offense. Bucky Irvin is a great back, but Bijan Robinson is an elite player. The rainy weather might keep the score down in this one, and it could help negate the Falcon's advantage through the air. Surely, Lucy keeps the football in place for Charlie Brown this time. Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 16 Gerald Thomas, III (3-4) Falcons-Buccaneers matchups always deliver compelling storylines, and Sunday’s meeting is no exception. There is Kevin Stefanski facing Baker Mayfield, Michael Penix Jr. making his long-awaited return to Tampa and Zac Robinson now serving as Atlanta’s offensive coordinator. Both teams enter the matchup following statement victories. Atlanta knocked off the previously undefeated 49ers, while Tampa Bay dominated the Panthers. A win would give the Falcons an opportunity to take over the top spot in the NFC South and continue building on their recent success. Prediction: Falcons 27, Buccaneers 17 Jerry Jones, Falcons Podcast (3-4) 99% of Falcons fans have deep-seated trauma, and games like this are exactly why. The Falcons are fresh off a win against arguably the best team in football and are facing a team that’s struggling. These are exactly the games the Falcons have inexplicably lost in recent years. That said, this is not a one-sided matchup. The Buccaneers are much better than their record suggests. They have a really good defense and have been excellent in the trenches on both sides of the ball. On top of that, all of the Buccaneers’ losses have been one-score games against teams above .500. I think this game will come down to how the Falcons’ o-line fares against the Bucs’ d-line. Michael Penix Jr. is an above-average quarterback when he’s playing ahead of the sticks and has a clean pocket. The other question is whether this o-line can create running lanes against one of the best run-defending d-lines in the league. I’m much more confident in how the Falcons’ defense stacks up against the Bucs’ offense. The defensive line has been playing great, and the Bucs’ banged-up receiving corps is overmatched against the Falcons' secondary. Ultimately, I have the Falcons winning this, but I think it will be a closer matchup than most expect. Prediction: Falcons 23, Buccaneers 20 Darius Hayes (3-4) I expect a tough, physical divisional battle with the weather playing a major factor in Sunday’s outcome. The Falcons should lean heavily on their running game to control the clock, establish the pace and keep Tampa Bay’s offense off the field. You can safely assume head coach Todd Bowles will dial up the heat on Atlanta, play press coverage on the outside to take away Penix's first read, and force him into mistakes under pressure. I trust this Tampa Bay defense, which ranks in the top five in DVOA against both the pass and the run. The Buccaneers are second in EPA per dropback and fifth in Rush EPA. If you want to stop Atlanta, you have to stop Bijan Robinson , and this Buccaneers defensive front has excelled at stopping the run for years. At 2-5, the Bucs have been left for dead more than once this season. However, their 43-13 annihilation of the first-place Carolina Panthers has them right back in the thick of the division race. Now only one game out of first place, Tampa's season has officially risen from the dead. If the Bucs can beat the 3-4 Falcons on Sunday, they will be only half a game behind the Panthers, who fell to 3-4 with their loss to the Green Bay Packers on Thursday. However, securing a victory over Atlanta will be no easy task. The Falcons are marching into Raymond James Stadium on a high note after their 29-20 win over the previously unbeaten San Francisco 49ers last week. This crucial NFC South showdown will have a big say in who takes the division crown this season and features two teams that have walked similar paths through the season's first seven weeks. The Bucs and Falcons both had high expectations coming into the season. Both teams have talented rosters and were hoping to break free of their recent curse of mediocrity. Like the Bucs, the Falcons fell flat coming out of the gate. After two straight losses to start the season, including an embarrassing 34-3 home defeat to the Panthers in Week 2, Atlanta looked like the league's worst team. However, those losses came with starting quarterback Michael Penix Jr. and backup Tua Tagovailoa both injured. The Falcons were forced to start third-string Cooper Rush in the first two games before he was benched for Jack Strand. Penix returned in Week 3 and led Atlanta to a dominant 35-14 win over the Packers at Lambeau Field, followed by a 45-24 thrashing of the New Orleans Saints on the road in Week 4. In those victories, plus last week's triumph over the 49ers, the Falcons have looked like a legitimate playoff team. The Bucs have also looked like a bottom-feeder for much of the season. However, in their demolition of the Panthers and a Week 5 road upset over the Dallas Cowboys , the Bucs have also looked like a playoff team. Both teams have taken turns as Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde this season. Which version of each team will we see on Sunday? In my five keys to a Buccaneers' victory , I highlighted the need for Tampa's defense to contain superstar Atlanta running back Bijan Robinson and to find a way to stop tight end Kyle Pitts, who has been a Buc-killer his entire career. If the Bucs can do both, they have a great chance to earn their third victory of the season. If not, it could be a long afternoon for the home team. The Bucs must also give their own star RB, Bucky Irving, a healthy workload to control the clock and keep the potent Atlanta offense on the sidelines. If Irving gets 20+ touches and Baker Mayfield takes care of the ball in his second game back from a three-game absence with a broken thumb, the offense should have success. I believe the Bucs' defense, which has been strong all year, will slow the Falcons offense just enough for Tampa to get its second straight victory. I think a late Penix interception will seal the game for the Bucs. Prediction: Bucs 30, Falcons 24

Charlie Disturco Sun, November 1, 2026 at 3:53 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Indianapolis Colts (2-5) take on the Jacksonville Jaguars (4-2) today in NFL Week 8. Kickoff is set for 1 p.m. ET from EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville, Fla. The game will broadcast live on CBS. The Jaguars are 10.5-point favorites on the spread, with an over/under of 46.5 points. Jacksonville is a -560 favorite on the moneyline while Indianapolis is a +420 underdog. Let's get into my Colts vs Jaguars prediction and player prop pick for today's game. Colts vs Jaguars pick: Bhayshul Tuten Over 64.5 Rushing Yards (-111, Up to 69.5) My Colts vs Jaguars best bet is on Tuten to record 65+ rushing yards, with the best price currently available at DraftKings. Make sure to find the best odds by checking our live NFL odds page. Download the Action Network app now for more NFL picks and analysis! Colts vs Jaguars Odds Colts vs Jaguars Spread : Colts +10.5 (-115), Jaguars -10.5 (-105) Colts vs Jaguars Moneyline : Colts +420, Jaguars -560 Colts vs Jaguars Total : 46.5 Colts vs Jaguars Preview The fire sale is officially on in Indianapolis. Following a third consecutive loss, the Colts traded away Quenton Nelson ( Seahawks ) and DeForest Buckner ( 49ers ). Josh Downs has also requested a trade, while all eyes have shifted toward the team's prized possession: superstar running back Jonathan Taylor . For now, there are no expected changes at quarterback. Colts head coach Shane Steichen doubled down on Daniel Jones , who threw for just 108 yards last week. The veteran quarterback has struggled mightily this season, throwing more interceptions (7) than touchdowns (4) while posting a career-low completion rate of 59.6%. There is some positive news for Indianapolis, however. Tyler Warren is expected to return to the starting lineup after missing two games with a groin injury. The same goes for Sauce Gardner , while Downs will also suit up despite his trade request. Warren's presence is a must for a Colts receiving room that includes 34-year-old Keenan Allen and journeyman Laquon Treadwell . The question remains: Can the Colts weather the storm and put up a fight against their division rival? The biggest question is how the offensive line will hold up against a formidable Jaguars defense. Indianapolis ranks around league average in rushing yards per game, but those numbers came with Nelson anchoring the offensive line. Taylor is already averaging a career-low 4.2 yards per carry, and losing another key piece up front certainly won't help. The Colts defense has its own issues, ranking in the bottom 10 in points allowed per game and 11th in rushing yards allowed (124.4). Rush defense is definitely Indy's Achilles' heel on the defensive end, ranking 29th in rushing EPA allowed. The pass defense, however, has been surprisingly solid. Indianapolis hasn't allowed a wide receiver room to reach 100 receiving yards since Week 4, while opposing receivers are averaging just 10 receptions per game. It was a much-needed bye week for the Jaguars, who are coming off two London games filled with late-game theatrics. Jacksonville's defense has been its strong suit this season. Outside of the Texans (34 points), no team has scored more than 17 against this talented unit. The Jaguars rank No. 1 in rushing yards allowed per game (72.2) but have struggled mightily against the pass, ranking 30th while surrendering 274 yards per game. Ultimately, Jacksonville's success will hinge on Trevor Lawrence and the offense finding another gear. The Jaguars are around league average in total offensive production and have maintained a near 50-50 split between the passing and running games. I'd be surprised if Jacksonville's ground game doesn't start to take off soon as Bhayshul Tuten is on the verge of a breakout. The explosive running back possesses elite speed and has already shown the ability to rip off chunk plays. Unfortunately, several of those big gains have been wiped away by holding penalties. Still, Tuten has rushed for at least 65 yards in five of his six games this season. I've been waiting for this offense to take the next step, and there are plenty of weapons to make it happen. Outside of Tuten, Jacksonville has a talented receiving corps led by Parker Washington . We also saw Travis Hunter become more involved offensively before the bye, recording four catches for 59 yards and a touchdown. That increased usage is a trend I expect to continue in Week 8. Brian Thomas Jr. has also been the subject of trade speculation ahead of the upcoming deadline. He was benched for the second half against Houston and hasn't recorded a catch in either of Jacksonville's last two games, making his involvement worth watching. One situation worth monitoring is Jakobi Meyers , who enters Sunday questionable after missing Friday's practice with hamstring and ankle injuries. Thomas would likely be relied on to step up in his absence. Another development I've highlighted previously is Jacksonville's increased use of two-tight-end sets. Brenton Strange has been nothing short of excellent, but the emergence of Nate Boerkircher could be just as important moving forward. The second-round pick played a career-high 55% of the snaps before the bye, and I expect his workload to consistently settle in the 50–60% range. Colts vs Jaguars Player Prop Pick I hinted at it earlier, but I expect the Jaguars' ground game to take off. To me, it's a matter of when, not if. Tuten is PFF's No. 1-ranked running back and ranks among the league's best in yards after contact per carry. He draws a Colts run defense that has struggled all season and will be without one of its most important defensive players in Buckner. With Jacksonville entering this matchup as a double-digit favorite, I expect the Jaguars to control possession and lean heavily on the ground game. That should mean a healthy workload for Tuten. Coming off a bye, Tuten should be fresh and ready to take advantage of a spiraling Colts squad. Don't be surprised if he finally breaks the 100-yard rushing mark in this one. home.headline: Colts, Jaguars Mid-Week Injury Reports Ahead of Divisional Showdown: CJ Allen's First Start?
home.blurb: After a walkthrough Wednesday, the Colts received encouraging news Thursday, with cornerback Sauce Gardner, guard Matt Goncalves, wide receiver Anthony Gould, and defensive tackle Tim Smith all upgrading to full participation. Gardner missed last week with a calf injury, so his return is crucial for a secondary that's been banged up in recent weeks. Tight end Tyler Warren remains limited with a groin injury after missing the last two games, making Friday's practice an important checkpoint for his potential return. Veteran cornerback Cam Taylor-Britt was placed on Injured Reserve earlier this week, keeping him out for at least the next four games. Although the Colts are set to have their starting outside duo available in Sauce Gardner and Charvarius Ward, the slot role remains up for grabs. If Walley cannot go, the Colts may turn to rookie UDFAs Kapena Gushiken or Kenneth Harris. Both young defenders have flashed at times this season, but neither has carved out a definitive role. Allen was kept out of most training camp with lingering injuries (groin, hamstring), which led to defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo turning to veterans Akeem Davis-Gaither and Jaylon Carlies while the rookie is slowly but surely ramped up. The Jaguars had two players upgrade to full participation Thursday, with cornerback Montaric Brown and tight end Brenton Strange both practicing without restriction. Brown was limited Wednesday with a hamstring injury, so his progress is notable. Brown's availability would give Jacksonville another option in the secondary against Indianapolis' passing attack. home.blurb: Jaguars-Colts Final Injury Report: Antonio Johnson Ruled Out - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Jaguars-Colts Final Injury Report: Antonio Johnson Ruled Out The Jacksonville Jaguars secondary could be stretched Sunday, as the team has ruled out safety Antonio Johnson for Sunday's Week 8 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts. Johnson (ankle) did not practice on Friday after initially suffering his ankle injury in the second quarter of the team's Week 6 London matchup versus the Houston Texans. His absence clearly puts more pressure on a safety room that has already dealt with attrition earlier this season with Eric Murray, who dealt with a Week 4 concussion that kept him out of Week 5. Those combined injuries, between weeks 5 and 6 resulted in safety Kaevon Merriweather playing increased snaps on defense: With Johnson now out, the expectation is that Merriweather will receive his first start of the 2026 season. Liam Coen discussed Merriweather in Friday's media availability. In addition to the Johnson update, wide receiver Jakobi Meyers (hamstring/ankle) also did not practice on Friday and is listed as questionable, though he spoke with Florida Times Union's Demetrius Harvey following practice, advising that he "felt okay." Meyers was listed on Wednesday and Thursday's injury report as a limited participant with only a hamstring issue, before sitting out Friday's session with an additional ankle issue that would have presumably occurred on Thursday. His status could come down to game day, with rain and a wet field in the forecast for Sunday. Running back LeQuint Allen Jr. (hamstring), defensive end Josh Hines-Allen (ankle), linebacker Jahlani Tavai (hamstring), and long snapper Ross Matiscik (shoulder) were all limited on Friday and carry no game-day injury designation. Additionally, cornerback Montaric Brown (hamstring), defensive tackle Ruke Orhorhoro (ankle), and tight end Brenton Strange (eye) were each full participants and expected to play. Notably, there has been no update on the 21-Day windows being opened for offensive lineman Patrick Mekari (back), rotational edge BJ Green (elbow), or rookie defensive end Zach Durfee (upper body). Each player has been on the injured reserve for at least four weeks, with the potential to return as the team comes off the Week 7 bye week. The Colts, on Friday, ruled out wide receiver and starting punt returner Anthony Gould (concussion). Gould is out even though he practiced fully on Thursday and Friday. Additionally, starting slot cornerback Justin Walley (knee) is out Sunday after not practicing all week. Starting linebacker Bryce Boettcher (groin) and tight end Drew Ogletree (knee) are both questionable. Boettcher has not practiced all week. Here are five predictions to accompany such bold thinking. Williams and Corum go for over 100 yards each Kyren Williams and Blake Corum went for 99 and 93 yards, respectively, against the Las Vegas Raiders last week. Now against a Chargers team that has yet to display the ability to engineer winning drives, there's no reason for the Rams to attack the air unnecessarily. It would not be shocking to see them get at least 18 carries each, and with their offensive line and tight ends leading the way, the yardage should be easy to find. Donald has his day The Chargers' interior offensive line is horrible, and even if they triple-team Aaron Donald, I still don't think they could stop him. Quarterback Justin Herbert always steps up in the pocket, and sometimes he runs into his own linemen. Thus, Donald should be in position to not just record his first sack since returning, but to have two on the day. Curl picks off Herbert Kam Curl has been the undervalued backbone of the Rams' defense, being able to play in a variety of spots, really taking the involvement of the safety to the next level in Chris Shula's scheme. He's a natural safety blanket to prevent the big play, and Herbert has been throwing questionable balls all year. Curl should snag one of those misfires. Stafford continues to slice and dice When the Rams revert to their balanced offense, Matthew Stafford's passing yards may not be as high as they once were, but his efficiency goes through the roof. His ability to read defenses, operate play action, and be comfortable with having his back turned to the defense has been the perfect pairing for their 12 and 13 personnel offenses. Stafford tosses three scores, while hitting eight different pass catchers on the day. He also has over 22 completions. The spookiest scenario comes to life With kicker Joshua Karty back in the fold, no one outside of the organization really knows what things will look like with current starter Brandon McManus. Is McManus the kicker, and is Karty doing kickoffs? Is there a certain range that the Rams trust Karty with more? To spice things up, I predict McManus misses at least one field goal or extra point to make the conversation even more interesting heading into November. away.headline: Chargers Announce Crushing Derwin James Jr. Injury Decision Before Week 8 vs. Rams
away.blurb: The Chargers officially placed star safety Derwin James Jr. on injured reserve Saturday, locking him out for at least four games after a major setback in his hamstring rehab. The entire plan was for the 15-day break to serve as his ramp-up period, but instead of making progress, he hit a brutal setback during practice reps coming out of the bye . What was supposed to be a short-term soft tissue issue exploded into a four-game mandatory IR stint, shutting down the pulse of this defense until late November. James will have to sit out a minimum of four games for the Chargers. To fill out the roster gap, the Chargers signed cornerback Isas Waxter to their active roster, while also elevating CB Kaiir Elam from the practice squad. Locked out until at least Week 12 against New England , James' absence leaves an 0-6 roster without its core player during the most critical month of the season. By the time he returns, there won't be much left for the Bolts. home.headline: Rams Sunday morning notebook: Optimism grows for Myles Garrett return, trade buzz heats up
home.blurb: Rams Optimistic Myles Garrett Will Return to Practice in Week 9 A story that continues to drag on for the Rams is when edge rusher Myles Garrett will finally return to the field. Garrett has been on injured reserve since before Week 2, and the timeline for his return continues to get pushed back. However, on Sunday, NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport reported that the Rams are optimistic Garrett will return to practice for Week 9. “Once again, there is optimism that Myles Garrett will return to practice this week. I know there was optimism last week, much more this week,” said Rapoport. “He should practice and should be on the field playing relatively quickly.” It’s worth noting that Rapoport reported last week that Garrett would return to practice. There is also a key distinction with this report. Rapoport simply reported that there is optimism for Garrett to return to practice. With Garrett on injured reserve, the Rams have the ability to open his 21-day practice window. That allows Garrett to practice for up to 21 days until the team has to decide to elevate him to the roster. With that being said, even if the Rams activate Garrett’s practice window, that doesn’t mean he would play next week. Given how safe the Rams have played it with Garrett, they could activate his practice window, see how his knee responds to being back in action, and then proceed from there. That’s not to say that Garrett won’t play next week, but a return after the bye remains more realistic. If the Rams open his 21-day practice window this week, they could wait until ahead of their Week 12 matchup with the Green Bay Packers to activate him. There is some thought that the Rams could try to trade for a wide receiver. However, things have remained quiet on that front as Les Snead waits for the market to shake out. One name who has been connected to the Rams is Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs . However, given the Rams’ struggles in kickoff coverage, the Rams may use Karty solely on kickoffs. Karty found success with a “knuckleball” kickoff last season, making it difficult for opposing teams to handle kickoffs. With Karty, the Rams allowed a league-best 17.7 yards per return. The Rams won't want to activate two kickers on gameday all season. Karty only has three eligible practice squad elevations. Ideally, the Rams can activate Karty for the next three games and become comfortable enough with him to eventually take over field goal duties as well. This is certainly going to be a situation to watch, especially as the Rams get healthier going forward and roster spots get more limited. Once that happens, it would be very difficult for the Rams to have two kickers active. Could Ejiro Evero Eventually Return to the Rams? My ATS record this year is 43-61-3, which is a long way from .500. My straight-up record is 62-44-1. So this week, it's back to just picking the games. Forget all dogs. Trying to get to .500 makes me borrow a coaching cliché they all use. One game at a time. One week at a time. Turnaround time. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Baltimore Ravens at Buffalo Bills (-3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Lamar Jackson could be back for the Ravens, but how much will his injured ankle impact his ability to move? The Bills are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. Baltimore's defense was bad in the loss to the Bengals last week, but Buffalo's defense has been awful. Look for a shootout here with Josh Allen getting the best of it. Pick: Bills 35, Ravens 30 Tennessee Titans at Cincinnati Bengals (-10.5) The Titans are having major problems on offense, while the Bengals lit up the Ravens last week. Joe Burrow was special in the second half of that game and I think that will carry over here. Look for an offensive explosion from the Bengals as Burrow starts to get into the MVP talk. Pick: Bengals 36, Titans 10 Arizona Cardinals at Dallas Cowboys (-6.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys' offense came alive against the Eagles Monday night, especially on the ground, which isn't a good thing for an Arizona defense that is last in the league in scoring. The Dallas offense should roll and the Arizona offense won't be able to keep up. Dallas big — even on a short week. Pick: Cowboys 37, Cardinals 21 Minnesota Vikings at Detroit Lions (-3) The undefeated Vikings face a tough road game here against Detroit. The Lions offense against the Minnesota defense will be a treat to watch. Jared Goff is playing at a high level right now, but Minnesota's defense is the best in the league in terms of scoring. The Vikings offense is limited, but the Detroit defense has had major problems. But they were better last week, which I think carries over. Lions take it. Pick: Lions 23, Vikings 13 Las Vegas Raiders at New York Jets (-1.5) Kirk Cousins stays in as the starter for the Raiders, but teams have blitzed him the past two weeks. That could be a problem here since the Jets are a top-10 team in blitz percentage. The Raiders have struggled to stop opposing offenses, giving up 28.1 points per game, so look for Geno Smith to have success. Jets win it. Pick: Jets 27, Raiders 16 Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) This is a big game for the division lead in the AFC North. The Browns beat the Steelers earlier this year, but this will be a bigger challenge on the road. They are also playing consecutive road games, which will be a challenge. Look for Aaron Rodgers to play well as the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 24, Browns 20 Atlanta Falcons at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (-2.5) This is suddenly a big game in the NFC South with the Bucs upsetting Carolina last week and the Falcons upsetting the 49ers. The Tampa Bay running game has come alive, but Atlanta is stingy on the ground, giving up 3.8 per rush. That will mean this is a Baker Mayfield game. Tampa Bay gives up 3.5 per rush, which might make for tough going for Bijan Robinson. That's a problem for the Atlanta offense. Tampa Bay wins it. Pick: Bucs 23, Falcons 17 Indianapolis Colts at Jacksonville Jaguars (-9.5) The Colts are a mess; they are playing consecutive road games, and they haven't won at Jacksonville since 2014, when Andrew Luck was the quarterback. Oh, and they traded their best offensive lineman, Quentin Nelson. The Jaguars are coming off a bye, so they will be rested. This one will get ugly as the Jaguars bounce back from the loss to the Texans in London. Pick: Jaguars 30, Colts 16 Los Angeles Chargers (+6.5) at Los Angeles Rams Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The battle of Los Angeles isn't quite the game many expected before the season. The Chargers, coming off a bye, haven't won yet and the Rams have been a disappointment. But the Rams won last week at Las Vegas to seemingly right things. They will win here, but the rested Chargers will keep it close. Pick: Rams 23, Chargers 20 Kansas City Chiefs (-1.5) at Denver Broncos Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chiefs' offense was lifeless in Seattle on Sunday night and now faces a tough Denver defense. They have to find ways to get the running game going again with Kenneth Walker. Bo Nix showed some life last week in the victory over Arizona, but this Chiefs defense will be a challenge. Look for a low-scoring game won by Kansas City, with Walker getting going against Denver's defense, which gives up 4.6 yards per rush. Pick: Chiefs 19, Broncos 14 New England Patriots (-7) at Miami Dolphins The Dolphins won their first game last week and have been in a lot of their losses. But this New England team will be a challenge, even at home. The Patriots are coming off a bad road loss to the Bears, and they will be rested, having played on Thursday. The defense limits the Dolphins' offense, and Drake Maye will play well. New England wins it. Pick: Pats 28, Dolphins 14 Philadelphia Eagles at Washington Commanders (-5.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This might be an elimination game of sorts for these two. Both need a victory in the worst way — even in their horrible division. The Eagles are crippled by injuries, but Washington has plenty of their own. With the Eagles on a short week off a Monday night game and the Commanders off a bye, Washington will win it. Pick: Commanders 28, Eagles 16 Chicago Bears at Seattle Seahawks (-3) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are riding high behind Caleb Williams and an improved defense. But this is a tough road trip against a Seattle team that showed what it can do on defense by shutting down the Chiefs Sunday night. Seattle also got the running game going. The Seattle defense will slow down the Chicago offense, and the Seahawks will win it. Pick: Seahawks 24, Bears 17 Carolina Panthers at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime These two are both coming off losses. The Carolina loss featured the Bucs running over them for 258 rushing yards. It's been a problem all year. But the Packers don't run it very well, so something has to give. Carolina gave Jordan Love fits last year, but that will change here. Carolina gives up 27.7 points per game. Love lights them up and Josh Jacobs gets the run game going. Denver has weathered a very tough schedule to open the 2026 season, beating the Los Angeles Rams, Seattle Seahawks, Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Chargers and Arizona Cardinals to begin the year at 5-2. While Denver’s offense has not been great (22nd in EPA/Play), the defense is a top-10 unit once again. Nix and Co. seemed to find a rhythm in a win over Arizona in Week 7, and they’ll look to carry that into a home date against Mahomes and the one-loss Chiefs. Kansas City dominated Denver at home in Week 1, winning by three touchdowns, but it’s coming off a shaky performance against the Seattle Seahawks in a loss in Week 7. The Chiefs are still 5-1 this season, but they scored just three points in their last game and failed to reach the red zone on a single possession. Will a Denver defense that has been red hot in recent weeks be able to slow down Kenneth Walker III and this Chiefs attack? All season long, the SI Betting team has been sharing final score predictions as a fun way to help bettors decide on their spread, moneyline and total bets. Plus, we’ve hit a few exact scores, which can make for a fun long shot bet from time to time during the season. With a ton at stake in this matchup – including first place in the AFC West – here’s a look at my prediction for the Chiefs vs. Broncos rematch in Week 8. Chiefs vs. Broncos Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Chiefs -1.5 (-105) Broncos +1.5 (-115) Broncos: -102 40.5 (Over -112/Under -108) There hasn’t been much movement in the odds for this game, as the Chiefs opened as 1.5-point road favorites even with their loss to Seattle on Sunday night. The total has dropped a point from 41.5 to 40.5, and it’s worth noting that the UNDER hit in this matchup in Week 1 with the Chiefs winning 31-10. Chiefs vs. Broncos Score Prediction This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shared his favorite bet for every single game in his Road to 272 column , and he’s buying the Chiefs on the road in this AFC West showdown: The Broncos' offensive issues and Bo Nix's play are going to haunt them against a good defense sooner rather than later. Their offense is 23rd in EPA per play and 29th in success rate, making them one of the worst offenses in the league through the first seven weeks. Now they take on a Chiefs team that has been impressive defensively, ranking fifth in both opponent EPA per play and opponent success rate. I'd like to see the Chiefs' offense lean on the run game even more moving forward, as they rank in the top three in every offensive rushing metric. They can use that weapon against a Broncos defense that has struggled to stop the run compared to recent seasons. They're 27th in opponent rush EPA. If the Chiefs can lean on their run game and continue to play good defense, they're going to get the road win and cover the short spread. A lot of this game comes down to two things: Do you believe in the Denver offense after a strong Week 7? And, how much stock do you put into Kansas City’s Week 1 win at home? The Broncos are still just 22nd in EPA/Play, 29th in success rate and 26th in yards per play on offense. That isn’t going to cut it against Patrick Mahomes and Kenneth Walker III, especially since Denver is allowing 4.6 yards per carry on defense. These teams are No. 5 (Kansas City) and No. 6 (Denver) in EPA/Play on the defensive side of the ball, and the UNDER has hit in the majority of both of their games. I expect another low-scoring affair with the Chiefs’ offense ultimately being the better unit on Sunday. Before Andy Reid's squad could even blink, the Chiefs are suddenly in danger of surrendering the AFC West lead when they take on the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High tomorrow. These division rivals have already faced off earlier this season, when Kansas City took care of business 31-10 in the regular season opener. However, the Broncos have strung together a three-game winning streak during which they have allowed fewer than 16 points per contest. Many Chiefs fans have grown increasingly concerned about the state of the offense after its horrendous three-point showing on Sunday Night Football . When opposing defenses take away Kenneth Walker, KC has struggled to get anything going and create explosive plays. This will undoubtedly be the most pivotal game of the Chiefs' season to date. Let's dive into what the ESPN Matchup Predictor believes will transpire in this AFC West clash. Chiefs at Broncos: ESPN Matchup Predictor Gives Prediction Even with a comparable record on paper, the matchup predictor still gives the Chiefs a slight edge tomorrow evening. Sep 14, 2026; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (15) throws a pass against the Denver Broncos during the game at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Denny Medley-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect ESPN Matchup Predictor Chances at Victory: Chiefs 55.7%, Broncos 44.0%. ESPN Matchup Predictor Chances at Victory: Chiefs 55.7%, Broncos 44.0%. The Chiefs have now been matchup predictor favorites in every game they've played this season. Chiefs on SI's Take Amid a week filled with the Chiefs being embroiled in controversy , it's important to remember that a crucial contest awaits them. They desperately need to avoid falling in their second consecutive loss and relinquishing the division lead. Things can only trend upward for this Chiefs offense, which mustered up 213 total yards and one field goal a week ago. Now that the outside noise about Kenneth Walker's return to Seattle can be put to bed, the hope is that he and Patrick Mahomes will get back to what they were doing earlier this year. As for Denver, much has been made about Bo Nix and his inability to move the ball downfield, but the Broncos have been winning in spite of his questionable quarterback play. His defense bailed him out time and time again in an overtime thriller two weeks ago, when the Broncos outplayed the Seahawks and won on a walk-off field goal by Wil Lutz. Ja'Quan McMillian read this PERFECTLY. SEAvsDEN on Prime Video Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1igvuDtROG It makes you wonder how a team that ranks in the bottom three of the NFL in offensive yards has a 5-2 record with several solid wins. While the Broncos look mediocre using the eye test, their record keeps proving everyone wrong. There's no question that the Chiefs have the better offense of these two teams, but the bigger question is whether they can find their footing early or if Denver's defense will stifle it from the jump. If the Broncos can force the Chiefs into playing their brand of football and turn this into a closely contested, defense-oriented matchup, that's where things could get dicey for KC. away.headline: Justin Tucker Returning To NFL, Joins Kansas City Chiefs
away.blurb: Justin Tucker Returning To NFL, Joins Kansas City Chiefs - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Week 8 Fantasy Football Toolkit Justin Tucker Returning To NFL, Joins Kansas City Chiefs Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Former All-Pro kicker Justin Tucker is returning to the NFL at the age of 36. Tucker is considered to be one of the greatest kickers in NFL history, which makes sense considering he's made 89.1% of his field goal attempts. His time with the Ravens ultimately came to an end after he was accused of inappropriate behavior during massage sessions. The Baltimore Banner reported that 16 massage therapists made accusations against Tucker, with two of the massage parlors claiming they banned him because of his behavior. "I did not act inappropriately at any point before, during, or after a professional bodywork treatment session, nor have I ever been told I am unwelcome at any massage therapy provider," Tucker told OutKick . "I absolutely respect the massage therapy profession and more so the individuals who work as massage therapists." Tucker has conducted workouts with the Colts, Jets and Saints over the past two years. It wasn't until this Wednesday, however, that he landed a deal. According to Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star, the Chiefs are signing Tucker to their practice squad. BALTIMORE, MARYLAND – DECEMBER 12: Kicker Justin Tucker #9 of the Baltimore Ravens talks to his wife, Amanda Bass, before playing against the New York Jets at M&T Bank Stadium on December 12, 2019 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images)Patrick Smith/Getty Images Harrison Butker has made plenty of big-time kicks for the Chiefs over the past decade, but he seems to be on the decline. Butker has made 11 of 16 field goal attempts this season. He had two crucial misses on Sunday night against the Seahawks. If Tucker outperforms Butker at practice, he could end up starting as early as this Sunday against the Broncos.

away.headline: ‘I don't know if he plays for the Chiefs again' - NFL Insider drops troubling update on Kansas City Chiefs' Josh Simmons days after he lands on IR
away.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
away.blurb: The starting left tackle, Simmons, hasn’t played since mid-August. His only exception was a limited practice week ahead of Kansas City’s Week 6 game against the Los Angeles Chargers. The absence stems from a back injury that has been described as a bulging disc . The Chiefs placed Simmons on injured reserve after VP of Sports Medicine and Performance Rick Burkholder explained the injury . “Things happen,” Reid said . “That’s no reason he was put on IR. He’s got a bad back. He’s got to get that worked out. That’s the main thing.” “So the gist of the report was this: something I reported with Mike Garafolo on Sunday, as you mentioned, that Josh Simmons was asked to leave a team meeting by Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes,” Rapoport said . “It involved having his feet up on the desk. He said he needed to because of his back. He’s going through rehab, and they said, ‘Well, just get out of here and go rehab.’ He did not handle it well. He went and apologized after. “Then he was placed on injured reserve, and there are a lot of questions about Josh Simmons, who has as talented a left tackle as you could possibly get, he is a stud as a player. I don’t know if he plays for the Chiefs again. I don’t know when he plays for the Chiefs again. There’s nothing more important than protecting Patrick Mahomes. You have to believe in the person doing it, and until that happens, I don’t know that he’s out there.” That distinction matters. Teams will stand by a player through injuries and even through odd absences. However, that patience tends to run out once an organization believes the effort isn’t going both ways. That said, the old NFL adage has to matter at some point: Availability is the best ability. Simmons missed nine games in 2025, and he has already missed six more in 2026. That’s 15 missed games out of 23 possible. He’s played in just eight games since being selected with the last pick in Round 1 of the 2025 NFL Draft. He’ll miss at least three more games on injured reserve. So far, there’s been no indication Simmons will return to play in the 2026 NFL season. Perhaps Rapoport is trying to send a message to the young, talented Simmons on behalf of the Chiefs. The Kansas City Chiefs placed LT Josh Simmons on injured reserve after months of questions about his back. A tense team meeting has added another layer, and now one of the NFL’s top insiders has weighed in with a troubling update. The Josh Simmons situation continues to reach unprecedented heights of strangeness for the Kansas City Chiefs. Now, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport is adding a troubling new layer to the story, focusing on Simmons’ future in Kansas City. Team meeting frustrations change the context Shortly after the IR move, news broke about frustrations boiling over in a team meeting . Chiefs head coach Andy Reid and quarterback Patrick Mahomes both told Simmons to leave the meeting and seek treatment for his back after he put his feet up, which he claimed was due to the injury. Rice recorded 79 receptions for 938 yards and seven touchdowns in 16 games during his rookie season in 2023. His reception and touchdown totals set Chiefs rookie records. He also had more than 100 receiving yards in two games. In the playoffs, Rice caught eight passes for 130 yards and two touchdowns against the Miami Dolphins in the Wild Card round. He finished the postseason with 26 receptions for 262 yards, setting franchise rookie records in both categories. Rice appeared in four games in 2024, recording 24 receptions for 288 yards and two touchdowns. In 2025, he played eight games and finished with 53 receptions for 571 yards and five touchdowns, along with 20 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown. With that in mind, I asked the following question this past week: What are your predictions, bold or otherwise, for the Miami Dolphins' defense and offense in this coming Sunday's game vs. the New England Patriots? Who do you expect to lead the team in key categories like tackles, tackles for loss, pass breakups, interceptions, defensive touchdowns, etc., on defense, and receiving yards, touchdowns, receptions, rushing production, and first downs, etc., on offense? What are your stat-line projections for our key playmakers this week, and/or who will be the team's MVPs on each side of the ball? Below are some of your takes and predictions for tomorrow's game- DalFinsFan is rightfully curious about this oddity in the schedule that seemingly helps a team from a colder climate that just happens to be the Pats. Curious why this is a late game instead of a 1:00pm ko. dedstrk says make it mistake-free and maybe? We need mistake free football and for the Pats to not take the Dolphins seriously enough for most of the game. Run the ball and continue on with the explosives and running the ball for first downs with Malik and OG. Phinette says the route to victory is keeping the ball out of the Pats' offense's hands. Our best shot at pulling off the upset is by controlling the clock. We need to stick with our ground game and avoid the costly three and outs. On defense we have to avoid being torched by the deep ball. If we can force the Pats to grind it out we have a shot. Phoenix6 has Miami narrowly edging out NE for victory #2. Defense: 1 sack, 1 fumble recovery, 2 interceptions. Rodriguez MVP. Offense: Ollie 89yds, 1 TD. Malik 289yds passing, 49yds rushing, 3 TDs. Douglas MVP. Dolphins 🐬 28, Patriots 27. coluccim believes that bad weather would be our best friend on Sunday. Our pass D is god awful, really. Pray for rain Phins1972 is much more focused on the rookies' development across the roster over the final score. We got our one win, and at this point I'm less concerned with the scoreboard than I am with seeing which players take a step forward and which ones don't. I really wish there were a young edge rusher on the roster who looked like a legitimate developmental piece. I'm still not a believer in Chop Robinson. He's played better lately, and credit where it's due, but I'm not sold yet. I'm interested to see whether Caleb Douglas can build on his recent performance and make an impact again. It would also be encouraging to see Chris Bell put together a solid outing. On the ground, I'd love to see Ollie top 100 yards once more. If Miami gets one of those hot, humid afternoons, a big back consistently moving the chains could have Patriots defenders gasping for air by the fourth quarter. If they can keep the game reasonably competitive, that'll be a positive. At this stage, player development is every bit as important as the final score, if not more so. Bill Hazlett has the defense doing their job well enough tomorrow to give us the W. Defense holds up. 28-17 Fins! JUK has Miami dropping this one by double digits. The Pats are clearly a stronger roster top to bottom. I think we will need to win the turnover battle to have a chance which has been the pats weakness but if Maye keep things clean they should win. It's likely to be a tough day for Willis if they get ahead too, as their secondary is so much stronger than our receiver room. We need to keep it close and run the ball well to have a chance. I'll say pats by 10 finfanfromsiam points to this team's long-standing issue covering any decent TEs. Does NE have TEs?? Nuff said…… CluelessNFLfan says that reality sets back in with another loss. The Phins come back down to earth this week. Pats 24, Phins 17. Robert Burstein has Miami losing by two TD's. I do think Miami can keep this game a little close until half time, but overall I think D.Maye will have a big game passing and making plays running. I've got Miami losing 13-27. Jptapt is being positive. Molly Polly II sees another upset on the horizon. I'm calling for an upset…why not! Patriots are favored +7.5. Defense tightens up shot group, Ollie beast mode another 100+ yards. Malik playing at home, confident, ready to prove he's the guy who can lead this team. Huge upset, Finz win with seconds left on the clock, 26-24! 🐬🐬 Gusman says it might be close, or Maye might just make the Dolphins' secondary look silly. If Drake Maye plays as he has for the past 4 games he should carve up the Dolphins secondary. Miami should be able to limit the Pats run game. Pats will attempt to shutdown Miamis run game forcing the Dolphins into passing situations. The Pats have a much better secondary than the Phins. Best bet for Miami is to hope Maye is sloppy and throws a couple picks and loses a fumble or two. The Pats are coming off a 10 day break and are not taking a Miami victory for granted. Should be a fairly close entertaining game. Well, the vote is split, with some of us agreeing with Vegas that the Dolphins are clearly set up for another loss, while others are feeling a bit more positive after pulling out the win last weekend against the NY Jets. As always, I want to thank each of you who makes an effort to join our discussions and answer our Phinsider Question Of The Day. Please join us tomorrow for full game coverage and, of course, the live game thread.

away.headline: Patriots hit with double dose of bad injury news day before Dolphins game
away.blurb: The Patriots listed running back TreVeyon Henderson as questionable to play the Dolphins due to an illness on the final injury report on Friday. New England also listed wide receiver A.J. Brown as questionable to play due to knee and ankle injuries. Both players did not participate in practice on Thursday or Friday. Per ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the Patriots downgraded Brown and Henderson to out on Saturday. Brown suffered a high-ankle sprain in the Patriots’ Week 1 loss to the Seattle Seahawks that kept him out until New England played the New York Jets in Week 6. On Friday, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said the knee injury Brown is dealing with this week is separate from the high-ankle sprain injury he suffered against Seattle. He wasn’t able to finish practice on Wednesday. “Just like everything else, when you come out of the game or a long week or practice on Monday, you evaluate the player,” Vrabel said , via the Patriots’ website. “He just wasn’t able to practice or finish practice on Wednesday. So, we’ll continue to treat him, and then we’ll see where he is tomorrow.” The New England Patriots will be down two key offensive players when they travel to play the Miami Dolphins on Sunday. More News: Exclusive: Breakout NFL Executives Who Could Become Future General Managers More News: 4 QBs Generating Serious Trade Buzz Weeks Before NFL Regular Season Starts Brown has nine receptions for 101 yards this season. New England traded a 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick to the Philadelphia Eagles for Brown in the offseason. Henderson has 203 yards rushing and one touchdown on 52 carries. The Patriots are 4-3 coming off a 30-24 loss to the Chicago Bears on “Thursday Night Football” in Week 7. Henderson had just nine yards on three carries against Chicago. Brown caught three passes for 88 yards. The Dolphins earned their first win of the season in Week 7 against the New York Jets. For more on the Patriots and the NFL , head to Newsweek Sports . away.headline: Patriots injury analysis: Pats get a much-needed reprieve in Week 7
away.blurb: The New England Patriots dropped to 4-3 on the year and out of the current AFC playoff picture with their loss to the Chicago Bears on Thursday night. However, not all was bad: the injury-ravaged team received a much-needed reprieve. S Kevin Byard III: Early in the second quarter, the veteran safety had to be checked out by trainers on the field due to an apparent left shoulder injury. He subsequently jogged off the field under his own power and into the blue medical tent, but reemerged after a brief evaluation. Byard ended up missing just four snaps before his return. He ended the game with a 94% playing time share , not missing any other reps down the stretch. The offseason trade acquisition has caught just six passes since his return from injury. Patriots injury analysis after Bears loss in Week 7 | Pats Pulpit Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A New England Patriots Community Pats Pulpit November 1, 2026 Pats Pulpit Notifications Notifications Sections News Notifications New England Patriots Injuries Analyzing the Patriots’ injury situation before their upcoming game against the Dolphins. In fact, there were only two noticeable injuries after rewatching the contest. Patriots injury analysis: NFL Week 7 DT Christian Barmore: Barmore made what could have been one of the biggest plays of the game in the late fourth quarter, sacking Caleb Williams for a 10-yard loss. Unfortunately, the play did not end up mattering — kicker Cairo Santos kicked a career-long field goal to effectively ice the game — while the sixth-year defensive tackle remained on the ground afterwards: he had landed awkwardly on his right hand and required medical assistance. home.blurb: A.J. Brown headlines the team’s questionable to face the Miami Dolphins after going from a limited participant to missing consecutive practices to end AFC East prep. The three-time All-Pro wide receiver is dealing with a knee issue that flared up while also working back from the high ankle sprain that sent him to injured reserve in September. “His status is questionable, like some other players,” head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters on Friday. “We’ll see how he comes in tomorrow and we’ll make a decision.” Running back TreVeyon Henderson, linebacker Christian Elliss and cornerback Carlton Davis III are also officially questionable for Sunday’s 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff at Hard Rock Stadium. While no Patriots have been ruled out for the divisional meeting, the Dolphins will be without the No. 12 overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft. Brown has played 101 out of 122 offensive snaps since being activated midway through October. The June trade acquisition has caught six passes for 75 yards through those two starts. And with fellow veterans Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins both on injured reserve , the Patriots stand with three healthy wide receivers on the 53-man roster in DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism III and Kyle Williams. “Just like everything else when you come out of the game or a long week, practice on Monday and evaluate the player. Just wasn’t able to finish practice on Wednesday,” Vrabel said. “So we continue to treat him and we’ll see where he is tomorrow.” On the defensive side of the questionable, Elliss has been a full participant with a chest injury for the past two weeks while Davis returned in full this week following a neck injury. The off-ball linebacker ranks atop the Patriots with 51 tackles through seven starts and has tacked on one sack, one forced fumble and a handful of quarterback hits. The cornerback, on the other hand, is on track for his return after missing three games in a row. “We’re really here focused on trying to get a win on the road in the division,” added Vrabel, “and we’ll make a decision on the guys that are questionable tomorrow.” The offseason trade acquisition has caught just six passes since his return from injury. away.headline: Eagles at Commanders Injury Report
away.blurb: RB Saquon Barkley against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 7 action After not practicing on Wednesday and Thursday with hamstring and back injuries, Saquon Barkley practiced in a limited capacity on Friday and is set to be available against the Commanders. The All-Pro running back missed two games with a hamstring injury before returning against the Cowboys on Monday night. However, Barkley was limited in the game after reaggravating his hamstring and injuring his back. "I feel decent. Good week of work, rehab, so I feel good to go back out there and practice," Barkley said after practice on Friday. "Being smart, listening to the trainers, listening to the strength guys and the strength staff, and just doing whatever I can to get back on that football field. That's what my motivation is. The team signed Jaydon Blue to the active roster after placing Dameon Pierce on Injured Reserve. Veteran running back Elijah Mitchell was elevated from the practice squad against the Commanders and could be elevated again this week if the Eagles desire three active running backs. Once Pierce exited the game, Mitchell made an impact receiving out of the backfield. Outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard was a full participant at practice while Jalyx Hunt remained limited. With Nolan Smith clearing concussion protocol, the Eagles will have all of their edge rushers available – a rarity this season. Defensive tackle Moro Ojomo was limited in practice all week with a neck injury, but will also be available against the Cowboys. "I feel like the last couple of weeks I've been dealing with different crap and I just want to feel healthy and just go out there and practice with those boys because practice is so important," Ojomo said on Friday. "So that's kind of been a pain, but the trainers have been great about that and coaches have been great about that." Return specialist Britain Covey (knee) has officially been ruled out of Sunday's contest, joining fellow wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), both of whom have not practiced for two straight weeks. On the defensive side of the ball, linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) and cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring) have been ruled out after not participating in practice all week. No players are listed as questionable. Safety Marcus Epps was added to the Eagles' injury report on Thursday with a jaw injury that required a concussion evaluation. He was officially limited in practice. Six players would not have practiced on Wednesday and those same six players did not practice on Thursday: running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back), linebacker Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), wide receiver/punt returner Britain Covey (knee), cornerback Jonathan Jones (hamstring), wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). home.headline: Commanders' final injury report takes a serious turn along defensive line
home.blurb: Javon Kinlaw missed practice all week, so it wasn't much of a surprise when the Washington Commanders officially listed him as out on their final injury report Friday. The surprise was Daron Payne , who was added with a foot injury; he's officially questionable after being limited in practice on the last day. John Bates, Treylon Burks, and Jer’Zhan Newton were all also listed as questionable for Sunday night's game against Philadelphia. Newton is still in his 21-day practice window as he returns from a pectoral injury ; the Commanders must still activate him before he's eligible. Bates improved from not practicing at all to limited, while Burks went from limited to not practicing , then back to limited on Friday . Commanders head coach Dan Quinn didn't hide how impressed he was with Newton's recovery work Wednesday: "Man, he has worked his ass off." Luke McCaffrey, Charles Omenihu , and Deatrich Wise Jr. were limited Friday but carried no game designation; Omenihu was limited all week with groin/ankle injuries. Nick Allegretti rebounded from missing Thursday's practice by returning as a full participant Friday. Jayden Daniels, Stefon Diggs, and Marcus Mariota all finished the week as full participants and carry no game designation. Philadelphia has its own injury problems , ruling out five players for Sunday night's game, including receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), Britain Covey (knee), Jonathan Jones (hamstring), and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). Cornerback Jakorian Bennett is questionable with a knee injury, while Saquon Barkley was limited Friday with hamstring/back issues but carries no game designation. Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) and Moro Ojomo (neck) were also limited but have no game designation. Commanders News: Treylon Burks Misses Practice With McLaurin Out Before Eagles Rematch | Burgundy Roundup UPDATE: Friday evening brought worse news. Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reported that Payne suffered a significant foot injury during practice and will miss Sunday's game. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo also reported that Payne could be headed to injured reserve, with further testing expected Saturday. home.blurb: RB Saquon Barkley against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 7 action After not practicing on Wednesday and Thursday with hamstring and back injuries, Saquon Barkley practiced in a limited capacity on Friday and is set to be available against the Commanders. The All-Pro running back missed two games with a hamstring injury before returning against the Cowboys on Monday night. However, Barkley was limited in the game after reaggravating his hamstring and injuring his back. "I feel decent. Good week of work, rehab, so I feel good to go back out there and practice," Barkley said after practice on Friday. "Being smart, listening to the trainers, listening to the strength guys and the strength staff, and just doing whatever I can to get back on that football field. That's what my motivation is. The team signed Jaydon Blue to the active roster after placing Dameon Pierce on Injured Reserve. Veteran running back Elijah Mitchell was elevated from the practice squad against the Commanders and could be elevated again this week if the Eagles desire three active running backs. Once Pierce exited the game, Mitchell made an impact receiving out of the backfield. Outside linebacker Jonathan Greenard was a full participant at practice while Jalyx Hunt remained limited. With Nolan Smith clearing concussion protocol, the Eagles will have all of their edge rushers available – a rarity this season. Defensive tackle Moro Ojomo was limited in practice all week with a neck injury, but will also be available against the Cowboys. "I feel like the last couple of weeks I've been dealing with different crap and I just want to feel healthy and just go out there and practice with those boys because practice is so important," Ojomo said on Friday. "So that's kind of been a pain, but the trainers have been great about that and coaches have been great about that." Return specialist Britain Covey (knee) has officially been ruled out of Sunday's contest, joining fellow wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), both of whom have not practiced for two straight weeks. Recovery runs on a sliding scale. A Grade 1 stretch heals in days to two weeks , a Grade 2 partial tear takes two to eight weeks, and a Grade 3 complete tear can sideline a player for six to 12 weeks or more, sometimes requiring surgery.
